湖南：禹貢荊州之域。 明屬湖廣布政使司，置偏沅巡撫。 清初因之。 康熙三年，析置湖南布政使司，為湖南省，移偏沅巡撫駐長沙。 雍正二年，改偏沅巡撫為湖南巡撫，並歸湖廣總督兼轄。 七年，置永順府，升岳州之澧州。 十年，升衡州之桂陽州。 乾隆元年，升辰州之沅州為府。 嘉慶二年，升辰州之乾州、鳳凰、永綏三廳。 二十二年，置晃州廳。 光緒十八年，置南州廳。 領府九，直隸廳五，直隸州四，屬州三，縣六十四。 東至江西義寧； 三百五十里。 西至貴州銅仁； 一千七百三十五里。 南至廣東連州； 八百二十里。 北至湖北監利。 三百五十里。 廣一千四百二十里，袤一千一百五十里。 北極高二十四度四十九分至二十九度三十七分。 京師偏西二度十四分至七度四十三分。 宣統三年，編戶四百二十八萬八千一百六十四，口二千二百五萬二千一百五十九。 其名山：衡岳、九疑、都龐、騎田、萌渚、幕阜。 其巨川：湘、沅、資、澧。 其澤：洞庭。 驛道：自長沙北達湖北蒲圻； 東南出插嶺關達江西萍鄉； 南達廣西全州； 西達貴州玉屏。 鐵路幹：粵漢中段。 支：萍株。 航路：自長沙南達湘潭，北達漢口。 電線：自長沙北達漢口，南通桂林，西通洪江，東通江西萍鄉、安源。
Hunan lay within the Jing region described in the Yu's Tribute. Under the Ming it fell under the Huguang Regional Administration Commission, which had a Pianyuan grand coordinator. The early Qing kept the same arrangement. In Kangxi 3 (1664) the Hunan provincial administration commission was split off as Hunan Province, and the Pianyuan grand coordinator relocated to Changsha. In Yongzheng 2 (1724) the post became the Hunan grand coordinator, concurrently overseen by the Huguang governor-general. In Yongzheng 7 (1729) Yongshun Prefecture was created and Lizhou in Yuezhou was promoted. In Yongzheng 10 (1732) Guiyangzhou in Hengzhou was promoted. In Qianlong 1 (1736) Yuanzhou in Chenzhou was raised to prefectural status. In Jiaqing 2 (1797) the Chenzhou departments of Qianzhou, Fenghuang, and Yongsui were all promoted. In Jiaqing 22 (1817) Huangzhou Department was established. In Guangxu 18 (1892) Nanzhou Department was established. The province comprised nine prefectures, five directly controlled departments, four directly controlled prefectures, three subordinate prefectures, and sixty-four counties. On the east, to Yining in Jiangxi; three hundred and fifty li. On the west, to Tongren in Guizhou; one thousand seven hundred and thirty-five li. On the south, to Lianzhou in Guangdong; eight hundred and twenty li. On the north, to Jianli in Hubei. Three hundred and fifty li. It measured one thousand four hundred and twenty li from east to west and one thousand one hundred and fifty li from north to south. North polar altitude ranged from 24°49′ to 29°37′. Longitude west of the capital ranged from 2°14′ to 7°43′. In Xuantong 3 (1911) registered households totaled 4,288,164 and population 22,052,159. Notable mountains included Mount Heng, Jiuyi, Dupang, Qitian, Mengzhu, and Mufu. Major rivers were the Xiang, Yuan, Zi, and Li. The great lake was Dongting. Postal routes ran from Changsha north to Puqi in Hubei; southeast through Chaling Pass to Pingxiang in Jiangxi; south to Quanzhou in Guangxi; and west to Yuping in Guizhou. The main railway was the middle Guangzhou–Hankou section. A branch ran Pingxiang–Zhuzhou. River traffic ran south from Changsha to Xiangtan and north to Hankou. Telegraph lines ran north from Changsha to Hankou, south to Guilin, west to Hongjiang, and east to Pingxiang and Anyuan in Jiangxi.

長沙府：沖，繁，難。 巡撫治； 布政、提學、提法三司，巡警、勸業、鹽法、長寶四道同治。 府隸之。 明隸湖廣布政使司。 康熙中，偏沅巡撫自沅州徙駐，為省治。 雍正二年改湖南巡撫。 東北至京師三千五百八十五里。 廣一千里，袤五百九十里。 北極高二十八度十三分。 京師偏西三度四十分。 領州一，縣十一。 長沙沖，繁，難。 倚。 東：天井。 西：谷山。 北：羅洋、石寶、麻潭、智度、銅山。 巨川則大江，洞庭湖匯湘、沅、資、澧入焉。 湘江自湘潭、善化入，納潦滸河及白沙河。 又西北，右合下泥港，左桐樹港，納八曲河，逕銅官山，至靖港，為古新康江口。 又西北，會喬口河，入湘陰。 瀏陽河在縣南，源出大圍山，西北流，經縣界入湘。 陶關在縣西南。 有喬頭鎮巡司。 喬頭、長沙二驛。 長株鐵路。 善化沖，繁，難。 倚。 南：昭山。 西：嶽麓。 西北：金盤。 東南：錫山，湘水在西，自湘潭入，西北流，左納觀音港，至瓦官口，靳江水從西南來注之。 北過水陸洲，入於長沙。 東：瀏渭水自瀏陽入，北合金塘港，至長沙入湘水。 又西，卯江水，一名滿官江，源出寧鄉嵇架山，東北與螺陂河水合，入長沙，是為八曲河。 南有暮雲市廢巡司。 有驛。 長株鐵路。 湘潭沖，繁，難。 府西南一百里。 西：烏台。 東：石潭。 南：曉霞。 東北：昭山，其下有昭潭。 西北：韶山。 西南：隱山。 東南：鳳凰山。 湘水自衡山入，東南流，過晚洲，屈而北，硃亭港水注之。 又東北，過淦田市，東與醴陵縣界。 又北，過空冷峽，又東北至於鑿石浦。 屈而西，涓水自西南來會。 水逕縣西易俗鄉，又名曰易俗河。 又北至湘河口，左合漣水。 又東北過縣治南，又西北為峨洲，入於善化。 其西靳江水自寧鄉入，迤東至善化入湘水。 二鎮：硃亭，縣丞駐； 下灄，舊有巡司，廢。 又永寧巡司亦廢。 黃茅巡司，乾隆二十六年置，後遷縣東株洲市，更名。 有南岸驛。 有商埠，光緒三十一年奏開。 有長株、株萍鐵路。 湘陰沖，繁，難。 府北一百二十里。 北：黃陵。 東：神鼎。 東南：玉池。 東北：汨羅山、玉笥山。 西北：錫山。 湘水在西，自長沙入，北合門涇江，又北流，西別出為濠河水，西北與資水分流，其合處曰臨資口。 其正渠又北至縣治西南，白水江注之。 又北過蘆林潭，錫江水合濠河水自西來會。 又北合汨水，西與湄水合。 又西北會羅水，為汨羅江，西北流，歧為二，至屈潭復合。 西北過屈羅戍南，分流注湘水。 湘水西北至磊石山，入於洞庭湖。 鎮三：營田，蕭婆、大荊。 縣丞治林子口。 西北有營田巡司，後廢。 新市、大荊鎮二巡司。 湘陰、歸義二驛。 寧鄉沖。 府西北一百里。 南：石鼓。 北：香林。 東：天馬。 東南：嵇山。 西：大溈山，溈水出，東南流，右納黃絹水，左瑕溪，至雙江口，流沙河水自西南來注之。 又東北，左合玉堂江水，右烏江水，又東北至縣治南，屈而東，會平江水，又東北入於長沙，為新康江。 又有靳江水在縣南，源出湘鄉，迤東至湘潭入湘。 有唐市鎮。 有驛。 瀏陽繁，疲，難。 府東一百五十里。 西：洞陽山。 北：道吾。 東北：大光山。 又大圍山，瀏水出，西南至雙江口，小溪水自東來會。 又過縣治西南，瀏渭水北流入焉。 又西與小河水合，西北入於長沙。 北：石柱峰，潦滸河出，西南流，屈西北至長沙為澇塘水。 又南川水即澄潭江，自江西萬載入，西南過江口入於醴陵，其下流是為淥水也。 永興、居仁二鎮。 梅子園一巡司，澄潭江，後遷縣西永安市。 醴陵簡。 府東南一百八十里。 北：小溈山。 東：王喬。 東南：大屏。 西南：君子山。 湘水瀆自湘潭入。 又南淥江水，有二源：北源曰南川水，自瀏陽入，西南至雙江口，萍水自南來會； 水出江西萍鄉縣，是為南源。 又西過縣治南，右納姜灣水，又西與鐵江水合。 水一名北江，自攸縣入，北合清水江，又北流為泗汾河。 水又北入淥水，至淥口入於湘。 有插嶺關。 淥口鎮巡司及驛，與醴陵驛為二。 株萍鐵路。 益陽沖，難。 府西北二百里。 北：五溪山。 南：小廬。 西：修山。 西北：紫雲。 西南：浮丘山。 益陽江在南，一名茱萸江，即資水，自安化入，東合泥溪、沾溪、桃花江、志溪諸水，過縣治南，別出為蘭溪水。 合喬江，東北流，北別出為甘溪，入沅江。 東有喬江水，首受資水，自沅江入。 西：西林港，歧為二，一東北入湘陰，一東南入長沙，皆合湘水。 北有益水，出五溪山，東與甘溪水合，至沅江入資。 有瓦湖鎮。 有驛。 湘鄉沖，疲，難。 府西南二百一十里。 北：仙女山。 東：東台。 西：石佛。 西北：靈羊。 西南有大禹山。 漣水一名湘鄉河，自邵陽入，北合金竹水，又北與藍田水會。 東北流，左納西陽水，屈東南至大江口，側水合崖源水自西南來注。 又東北過石魚山東，青陂水南流合焉，東北至湘潭入湘水。 虞塘、定勝二鎮。 縣丞治永豐市。 婁底巡司。 明置武障，乾隆三年徙改。 攸繁，疲，難。 府東南二百八十里。 東：司空。 東北：羅浮。 西北：明月山。 攸水在東，源出江西萍鄉縣西，合陽升江水，西南至縣治東南入洣水。 水自茶陵入，亦名曰茶陵江也。 洣水又西與陰山江合，入衡山。 東北有鳳嶺巡司，雍正十一年置。 安化簡。 府西二百六十里。 東：移風。 南：浮青。 北：大峰。 西北：小辰。 西南：大熊山。 山與新化接界。 資水在西，一名邵河，自新化入。 西北合渠水，屈東北流，過縣治北，屈而東，敷溪水自南來注。 又東納善溪水，入於益陽。 東南有藍田水，亦自新化入，東北至湘鄉入漣水。 又歸溪水，源出縣西司徒嶺，西南流，與湄江合。 屈東南，至湘鄉合藍田水。 茶陵州繁，難。 府東南四百八十里。 西：雲陽。 東：皇雩。 東北：景陽山，即茶山。 洣水自酃入，亦曰茶陵江，西北流，右納洮水，北過州治東，茶水自東北來注，又西北入攸。 有視渡口巡司，治州南視渡關，後遷高岡南關。
Changsha Prefecture was rated pivotal, busy, and difficult. Seat of the provincial grand coordinator; The civil administration, education, and judicial commissions, together with the constabulary, industry promotion, salt administration, and Changbao circuits, all shared the prefectural seat. The prefecture fell under their jurisdiction. Under the Ming it belonged to the Huguang provincial administration commission. In the Kangxi era the Pianyuan grand coordinator relocated from Yuanzhou, making it the provincial capital. In Yongzheng 2 the post was retitled Hunan grand coordinator. It lay three thousand five hundred eighty-five li northeast of the capital. It measured one thousand li east to west and five hundred ninety li north to south. North polar altitude was 28°13′. Longitude was 3°40′ west of the capital. It governed one subordinate prefecture and eleven counties. Changsha was rated pivotal, busy, and difficult. Attached to the prefectural seat. To the east: Tianjing. To the west: Gushan. To the north: Luoyang, Shibao, Matan, Zhidu, and Tongshan. The chief watercourse was the Yangzi; Dongting Lake received the Xiang, Yuan, Zi, and Li before emptying into it. The Xiang entered from Xiangtan and Shanhua, taking in the Liaoxu and Baisha rivers. Farther northwest it took Xiani Harbor on the right and Tongshu Harbor on the left, absorbed the Baqu River, passed Tongguan Mountain to Jinggang—the old mouth of the Xinkang River. Still farther northwest it met the Qiaokou River and entered Xiangyin. South of the county the Liuyang River rose on Mount Dawei, flowed northwest across the border, and joined the Xiang. Taoguan Pass lay southwest of the county. It had the Qiaotou garrison patrol office. Postal stations at Qiaotou and Changsha. The Changsha–Zhuzhou Railway. Shanhua was rated pivotal, busy, and difficult. Attached to the prefectural seat. To the south: Zhaoshan. To the west: Yuelu. To the northwest: Jinpan. Southeast lay Xishan; west of the county the Xiang entered from Xiangtan, flowed northwest, took Guanyin Harbor on the left to Waguan Mouth, where the Jin River joined from the southwest. Northward it passed Shuilu Isle and entered Changsha. To the east the Liuwei River came from Liuyang, merged with Jintang Harbor, and reached Changsha to join the Xiang. Farther west the Maojiang, also called Manguan River, rose on Jijia Mountain in Ningxiang, met the Luopi River northeast, and entered Changsha as the Baqu River. South lay the abolished Muyun Market patrol office. It had a postal station. The Changsha–Zhuzhou Railway. Xiangtan was rated pivotal, busy, and difficult. One hundred li southwest of the prefectural seat. To the west: Wutai. To the east: Shitan. To the south: Xiaoxia. To the northeast: Zhaoshan, with Zhaotan below it. To the northwest: Shaoshan. To the southwest: Yinshan. To the southeast: Fenghuang Mountain. The Xiang entered from Hengshan, ran southeast past Wan Isle, bent north, and received the Zhuting Harbor River. Farther northeast it passed Gantian Market and bordered Liling County on the east. It went north through Kongleng Gorge, then northeast to Zaoshi Ford. Bending west, it met the Juan River from the southwest. The stream crossed Yisu Township west of the county and was also known as the Yisu River. Farther north at Xianghe Mouth the Lian River joined on the left. It ran northeast past the south of the seat, then northwest as E Isle into Shanhua. Westward the Jin River entered from Ningxiang, wound east through Shanhua, and joined the Xiang. Two market towns: Zhuting, seat of the assistant magistrate; and Xialuan, where an old patrol office had been abolished. The Yongning patrol office was abolished as well. The Huangmao patrol office, established in Qianlong 26 (1761), was later moved to Zhuzhou Market east of the county and renamed. It had the Nan'an postal station. A treaty port was opened by memorial in Guangxu 31 (1905). The Changsha–Zhuzhou and Zhuzhou–Pingxiang railways served it. Xiangyin was rated pivotal, busy, and difficult. It lay one hundred twenty li north of the prefectural seat. To the north: Huangling. To the east: Shending. To the southeast: Yuchi. To the northeast: Miluo Mountain and Yujian Mountain. To the northwest: Xishan. The Xiang lay on the west: it entered from Changsha, met the Menjing River to the north, continued north, branched west as the Hao River, and parted from the Zi to the northwest at Linzikou. The main channel ran north to the southwest of the seat, where the Baishui River joined. Still farther north it passed Lulin Pool, where the Xi River—already merged with the Hao—came in from the west. Continuing north it took the Mi River, which had joined the Mei on the west. Farther northwest it met the Luo to form the Miluo River, flowing northwest in two branches that reunited at Qutan. Passing northwest south of Quluo Fort, it divided and fed the Xiang. The Xiang ran northwest to Leishi Mountain and entered Dongting Lake. Three market towns: Yingtian, Xiaopo, and Dajing. The assistant magistrate was stationed at Linzikou. To the northwest stood the Yingtian patrol office, later abolished. Patrol offices at Xinshi Market and Dajing Market. Postal stations at Xiangyin and Guiyi. Ningxiang County was rated pivotal. It lay one hundred li northwest of the prefectural seat. To the south: Shigu. To the north: Xianglin. To the east: Tianma. To the southeast: Jishan. To the west stood Mount Dawei; the Wei River rose there, flowed southeast, took the Huangjuan on the right and Xia Creek on the left, and at Shuangjiang Mouth received the Liusha from the southwest. Farther northeast it took the Yutang on the left and the Wujiang on the right, ran northeast to the south of the seat, bent east to meet the Ping River, and entered Changsha northeast as the Xinkang River. South of the county the Jin River rose in Xiangxiang, wound east to Xiangtan, and joined the Xiang. It had Tangshi Market. It had a postal station. Liuyang County was rated busy, exhausted, and difficult. It lay one hundred fifty li east of the prefectural seat. To the west: Mount Dongyang. To the north: Daowu. To the northeast: Daguang Mountain. Mount Dawei also stood there; the Liu River rose on it, flowed southwest to Shuangjiang Mouth, and met a brook from the east. It passed southwest of the seat as the Liuwei River entered from the north. Farther west it united with the Xia River and entered Changsha to the northwest. To the north, Shizhu Peak; the Liaoxu rose there, flowed southwest, bent northwest to Changsha as the Laotang River. The Nanchuan River, also called the Chengtan, entered from Wanzai in Jiangxi, ran southwest past Jiangkou into Liling—its lower reach was the Lu River. Market towns at Yongxing and Juren. A patrol office at Meiziyuan on the Chengtan was later moved to Yong'an Market west of the county. Liling County was rated simple. It lay one hundred eighty li southeast of the prefectural seat. To the north: Mount Xiaowei. To the east: Wangqiao. To the southeast: Daping. To the southwest: Junzi Mountain. A distributary of the Xiang entered from Xiangtan. Farther south was the Lu River with two sources: the northern, the Nanchuan, entered from Liuyang, ran southwest to Shuangjiang Mouth, and met the Ping from the south; That stream rose in Pingxiang County, Jiangxi—the southern source. Farther west it passed south of the seat, took the Jiangwan on the right, and joined the Tie River on the west. That stream, also called the Beijiang, entered from You County, met the Qingshui to the north, and flowed north as the Sifen River. It entered the Lu farther north, reached Lukou, and joined the Xiang. It had Chaling Pass. A patrol office at Lukou Market and a postal station, the second together with Liling's station. The Zhuzhou–Pingxiang Railway served it. Yiyang County was rated pivotal and difficult. It lay two hundred li northwest of the prefectural seat. To the north: Wuxi Mountain. To the south: Xiaolu. To the west: Xiushan. To the northwest: Ziyun. To the southwest: Fuqiu Mountain. South lay the Yiyang River—also the Zhuyu River, that is, the Zi—which entered from Anhua, took the Nixi, Zhanxi, Taohuajiang, and Zhixi from the east, passed south of the seat, and branched as the Lanxi. It met the Qiao River, ran northeast, and split north as the Gan River into the Yuan. To the east the Qiao River first took the Zi and entered from the Yuan. To the west, Xilin Harbor split: one branch ran northeast into Xiangyin, one southeast into Changsha—both rejoined the Xiang. To the north the Yi rose on Wuxi Mountain, met the Gan to the east, and at the Yuan entered the Zi. It had Wahou Market. It had a postal station. Xiangxiang County was rated pivotal, exhausted, and difficult. It lay two hundred ten li southwest of the prefectural seat. To the north: Xiannü Mountain. To the east: Dongtai. To the west: Shifo. To the northwest: Lingyang. To the southwest: Dayu Mountain. The Lian River, also the Xiangxiang River, entered from Shaoyang, met the Jinzhu to the north, and farther north united with the Lantian. It flowed northeast, took the Xiyang on the left, bent southeast to Dajiang Mouth, and there the Ce united with the Yayuan from the southwest. Farther northeast, past east of Shiyu Mountain the Qingbei joined from the south; northeast to Xiangtan it entered the Xiang. Market towns at Yutang and Dingsheng. The assistant magistrate was stationed at Yongfeng Market. It had the Loudi patrol office. Wuzhang was set up in the Ming and moved and reorganized in Qianlong 3. You County was rated busy, exhausted, and difficult. It lay two hundred eighty li southeast of the prefectural seat. To the east: Sikong. To the northeast: Luofu. To the northwest: Mingyue Mountain. East lay the You River, rising west of Pingxiang in Jiangxi, joining the Yangsheng, and reaching southeast of the seat to enter the Mi. The Mi entered from Chaling and was also called the Chaling River. The Mi united with the Yinshan on the west and entered Hengshan. To the northeast stood the Fengling patrol office, established in Yongzheng 11. Anhua County was rated simple. It lay two hundred sixty li west of the prefectural seat. To the east: Yifeng. To the south: Fuqing. To the north: Dafeng. To the northwest: Xiaochen. To the southwest: Mount Daxiong. The mountain formed the border with Xinhua. West lay the Zi River, also called the Shao River, entering from Xinhua. Northwest it united with the Qu, bent northeast past north of the seat, then east as the Fuxi joined from the south. Farther east it took the Shanxi and entered Yiyang. Southeast lay the Lantian, also entering from Xinhua and reaching the Lian at Xiangxiang to the northeast. The Gui River also rose on Situ Ridge west of the county, flowed southwest, and united with the Mei. It bent southeast to Xiangxiang and met the Lantian. Chaling Prefecture was rated busy and difficult. It lay four hundred eighty li southeast of the prefectural seat. To the west: Yunyang. To the east: Huangyu. To the northeast: Jingyang Mountain, also called Tea Mountain. The Mi entered from Ling, also the Chaling River, flowing northwest with the Tao on the right, passing east of the seat as Chashui joined from the northeast, then northwest into You. It had the Shidu Crossing patrol office at Shidu Pass south of the seat, later moved to Gaogang South Pass.
5
寶慶府：難。 隸長寶道。 舊隸湖廣布政使司，康熙三年來屬。 東北距省治五百里。 廣六百六十里，袤六百三十里。 北極高二十七度四分。 京師偏西五度六分。 領州一，縣四。 邵陽繁，難。 倚。 南：四望。 東：大雲。 東北有龍山。 西北：首望。 資水自武岡入，東納辰溪水，東北過府治北。 邵水出龍山，南合桐江、檀江，屈西北流注之，北與漁溪合。 西北會高平水，入新化。 又漣水亦出龍山，東北入湘鄉。 又烝水源出邪姜山，合大雲水，至衡陽入湘。 又西洋江出西北隆回鄉，南至武岡，流合洞口水。 有隆回巡司。 其黑田鋪巡司，乾隆二十五年置，後廢。 通判駐桃花坪。 新化繁，難。 府西北一百八十里。 北：大熊山。 東北有黃柏界山，皆與安化接界。 南：梅山、長龍。 西南：文仙。 西北：清虛，一名大西山。 資水在東，自邵陽入，西北過縣治北，雲溪水合洋溪自西南來注之。 又北與油溪水合，入安化。 西有渠江水，源出冷溪山，北至安化入資水。 東有藍田水，上源曰墨溪，出邵陽，亦入安化。 高平水出西南首望山，東南流，入邵陽，注資水。 西北有蘇溪鎮巡司，乾隆四十年廢。 城步難。 府西南四百二十里。 乾隆三年改隸靖州，七年復。 東：羅漢山。 東南：金紫山，與廣西全州接界。 西南：金童，又有藍山。 西北：楓門山。 東北：青角山，即古路山，資水所出，一名都梁水，又名濟水。 北流屈東，左會款溪水，入武岡。 又有巫水，源出東北巫山，南屈而西為漁渡江，縣東南諸水皆入焉。 至縣治西南，左納界背水，西北與清溪水合，入綏寧。 西南有長平水，又曰藍山水，亦入綏寧，為臨川水。 又有長灘水，出縣南，南至廣西龍勝廳，曰貝子溪，其下流是為潯江。 同官水亦南入龍勝，為太平溪，流合貝子溪。 有橫嶺峒巡司，本寨頭司，乾隆元年置，後遷橫嶺更名。 江頭汛巡司治莫宜峒，乾隆六十年置長安營，同知駐。 轄瑤峒五：曰蓬峒、牛欄、莫宜、扶城、橫嶺。 為寨四十有八。 武岡州繁，疲，難。 府西南二百八十里。 西北有武岡山，州以是名。 又西北，天尊山，山與綏寧接界。 南：雲山。 東南：寶方，又名資勝山。 資水在南，自城步入，東合威溪。 又東過州治南，左合渠水，右納石門水，又東北流，蓼溪水自西來會。 蓼溪一曰高沙市水，出綏寧。 又北合洞口水，水上源曰平溪，出黔陽。 東南流，右納岳溪水，東合西洋江，至平溪口入資水。 資水又北，屈而東，逕紫陽山，曰紫陽河，龍江水北流入焉。 又東南與夫夷水會，入邵陽。 西北：𦰡溪自綏寧入，至黔陽入沅水。 州同駐高沙市。 峽口、石門司二巡司。 紫陽、蓼溪二廢司。 新寧繁，難。 府西南三百里。 西：花溪。 南：金城。 西南：峎山。 東南：大雲。 東北：高桂。 又有紫雲山，山與武岡、東安接界。 夫夷水在南，一名羅江水，其上源曰西延水，自廣西全州入，東北流，左納深沖水，又北至縣治西南，新寨水自西來注之。 屈東過筆架山，合水頭水，又東北納涷江水，合小溪水，入武岡，為資水別源。 東有靖位鎮巡司，康熙二十三年廢。
Baoqing Prefecture was rated difficult. It was subordinate to the Changbao Circuit. Formerly under the Huguang provincial administration commission, it came under Hunan in Kangxi 3. It lay five hundred li northeast of the provincial seat. It measured six hundred sixty li east-west and six hundred thirty li north-south. North polar altitude was 27°4′. Longitude was 5°6′ west of the capital. It governed one subordinate prefecture and four counties. Shaoyang was rated busy and difficult. Attached to the prefectural seat. To the south: Siwang. To the east: Dayun. To the northeast: Mount Long. To the northwest: Shouwang. The Zi entered from Wugang, took the Chenxi on the east, and passed northeast of the seat. The Shao rose on Mount Long, joined the Tong and Tan to the south, bent northwest to enter the Zi, and north united with the Yu. Northwest it met the Gaoping and entered Xinhua. The Lian also rose on Mount Long and entered Xiangxiang to the northeast. The Zheng rose on Mount Xiejiang, united with the Dayun, and at Hengyang entered the Xiang. The Xiyang rose in northwest Longhui Township, flowed south to Wugang, and joined the Dongkou River. It had the Longhui patrol office. The Heitianpu patrol office was established in Qianlong 25 and later abolished. The subprefectural judge was stationed at Taohuaping. Xinhua was rated busy and difficult. It lay one hundred eighty li northwest of the prefectural seat. To the north: Mount Daxiong. To the northeast: Mount Huangbaijie; both mountains bordered Anhua. To the south: Meishan and Changlong. To the southwest: Wenxian. To the northwest: Qingxu, also called Mount Daxi. East lay the Zi, entering from Shaoyang and passing northwest of the seat as the Yunxi united with the Yangxi from the southwest. Farther north it united with the Youxi and entered Anhua. West lay the Qu, rising on Mount Lengxi and north to Anhua to enter the Zi. East lay the Lantian; its upper stream was the Moxi, rising in Shaoyang and also entering Anhua. The Gaoping rose on Mount Shouwang to the southwest, flowed southeast into Shaoyang, and entered the Zi. Northwest stood the Suxi Market patrol office, abolished in Qianlong 40. Chengbu was rated difficult. It lay four hundred twenty li southwest of the prefectural seat. In Qianlong 3 it was reassigned to Jingzhou and restored in Qianlong 7. To the east: Mount Luohan. To the southeast: Mount Jinzi, bordering Quanzhou in Guangxi. To the southwest: Jintong; there was also Mount Lan. To the northwest: Mount Fengmen. To the northeast: Mount Qingjiao, the ancient Lu Mountain, source of the Zi, also called the Duliang River and the Ji River. It flowed north, bent east, took the Kuanxi on the left, and entered Wugang. The Wu River also rose on Mount Wu to the northeast, bent south and west as the Yudu River, and all southeastern waters of the county entered it. At southwest of the seat it took the Jiebei on the left, northwest united with the Qingxi, and entered Suining. Southwest lay the Changping, also the Lanshan, which also entered Suining as the Linchuan. The Changtan also issued south of the county, south to Longsheng Subprefecture in Guangxi as the Beizi Stream; its lower course was the Xun River. The Tongguan also entered Longsheng to the south as the Taiping Stream and joined the Beizi. It had the Henglingdong patrol office, originally Zhaaitou Office, established in Qianlong 1, later moved to Hengling and renamed. The Jiangtou garrison patrol office administered Moyidong; in Qianlong 60 the Chang'an Garrison was established with an intendant stationed there. It governed five Yao dong: Pengdong, Niulan, Moyi, Fucheng, and Hengling. It had forty-eight stockades in all. Wugang Prefecture was rated busy, exhausted, and difficult. It lay two hundred eighty li southwest of the prefectural seat. To the northwest: Mount Wugang, which gave the prefecture its name. Farther northwest: Mount Tianzun, bordering Suining. To the south: Mount Yun. To the southeast: Baofang, also called Mount Zisheng. South lay the Zi, entering from Chengbu and uniting with the Weixi to the east. Farther east it passed south of the seat, took the Qu on the left and Shimen on the right, flowed northeast, and the Liaoxi met it from the west. The Liaoxi was also the Gaoshashi River, issuing from Suining. Farther north it united with the Dongkou; its upper stream was the Pingxi, rising in Qianyang. It flowed southeast, took the Yuexi on the right, east united with the Xiyang, and at Pingxi Mouth entered the Zi. The Zi again flowed north, bent east past Mount Ziyang as the Ziyang River, and the Longjiang entered from the north. Farther southeast it met the Fuyi and entered Shaoyang. To the northwest: Naxi Creek entered from Suining and at Qianyang entered the Yuan. The prefectural subprefect was stationed at Gaoshashi. It had the Xiakou and Shimen patrol offices. The Ziyang and Liaoxi offices were abolished. Xinning was rated busy and difficult. It lay three hundred li southwest of the prefectural seat. To the west: Huaxi. To the south: Jincheng. To the southwest: Mount E. To the southeast: Dayun. To the northeast: Gaogui. Mount Ziyun also stood on the borders with Wugang and Dong'an. South lay the Fuyi, also the Luojiang; its upper stream was the Xiyan, entering from Quanzhou in Guangxi, flowing northeast with Shenchong on the left, north to southwest of the seat as Xinzhai joined from the west. It bent east past Mount Bijia, united with the Shuitou, northeast took the Dongjiang and Xiaoxi, entered Wugang, and became a separate headwater of the Zi. East stood the Jingwei Market patrol office, abolished in Kangxi 23.
6
岳州府：沖，繁，疲，難。 隸岳常澧道。 舊隸湖廣布政使司。 康熙三年來屬。 初沿明制，領州一，縣七。 雍正七年，澧升直隸州，石門、安鄉、慈利割隸。 西南距省治三百里。 廣三百八十里，袤三百四十里。 北極高二十九度二十四分。 京師偏西三度三十四分。 領縣四。 同知一。 道光元年移治君山，後廢。 有岳州商埠，光緒二十四年奏開。 巴陵沖，繁，疲，難。 倚。 城內巴丘山。 東：大雲、銅鼓，皆與臨湘縣接界。 東南：靈屋、五龍。 大江在西北，洞庭湖在西南。 君山、扁山、石城山皆在湖中。 湖周八百餘里，南連青草，西接赤沙，謂之三湖，湘、沅、資、澧諸水咸匯焉。 東北至三江口，合大江，古謂之五渚。 大江又東北入臨湘。 有城陵磯，天險也。 南有新牆河，即微水，自臨湘入，西南流，左納沙港，迤西至灌口，入洞庭湖。 水出東南清水嶺，西南至湘陰合汨水。 㴩湖在東南，一名翁湖，又東為角子湖。 楊林街，縣丞。 鹿角鎮，主簿。 東：岳陽驛。 舊有青岡驛，順治十六年置，有丞，乾隆十六年裁。 臨湘沖，繁。 府東北九十里。 東：黃皋。 西南，微落。 東南：大雲。 又龍窖山，跨湖北通城、蒲圻諸縣，微水所出，迤西逕土城，左納馬港，西南入巴陵。 大江在縣西，自巴陵入，東北過彭城山，松陽湖水自東南來注之。 又東北與白泥湖水合，過鴨欄磯，入湖北嘉魚。 黃蓋湖在東北，縣東諸水皆匯焉，北注清江口，入大江。 東南有桃林、長安巡司，城陵磯，乾隆二十六年徙長安鎮，更名，尋復故。 雲溪、長安二驛。 鴨欄磯、長安二鎮。 華容疲，難。 府西北一百八十里。 北：黃湖。 東：石門、墨山。 東北：東山。 東南：鼓樓山。 大江右瀆自湖北監利入，東屈而南，入巴陵。 北華容河，西涌水，皆首受大江水，自湖北石首入，東南流入洞庭湖。 澧水在縣南，自安鄉入，合赤沙湖，亦注洞庭。 東北大荊湖及團湖，合流入大江。 黃家穴司巡司。 黃家、鼓樓二鎮。 平江疲，難。 府東南二百四十里。 北：永寧。 西：湖源。 東：道岩。 東南：連雲。 東北：幕阜山，一名天岳山，下有天岳關。 又有汨水，自江西義寧入，西南流，右納紅橋水，左納白鉛諸水，又西南至白湖口，屈而北，鍾洞水南流西屈注之。 又西合盧水，又西北與暹江水合，屈西南過縣治南，左納晉坑水。 又西北至將軍山，昌山自東北來會，迤西入於湘陰。 東有長壽巡司。
Yuezhou Prefecture was rated pivotal, busy, exhausted, and difficult. It was subordinate to the Yuechangli Circuit. Formerly under the Huguang provincial administration commission. In Kangxi 3 it came under Hunan. At first it followed the Ming arrangement, governing one subordinate prefecture and seven counties. In Yongzheng 7, Li was raised to a direct-controlled prefecture, and Shimen, Anxiang, and Cili were transferred to its jurisdiction. It lay three hundred li southwest of the provincial seat. It measured three hundred eighty li east to west and three hundred forty li north to south. North polar altitude was 29°24′. Longitude was 3°34′ west of the capital. It governed four counties. It had one associate prefect. In Daoguang 1 the seat was moved to Junshan, then abolished. The Yuezhou treaty port was opened by memorial in Guangxu 24. Baling was rated pivotal, busy, exhausted, and difficult. Attached to the prefectural seat. Within the city stood Mount Baqiu. To the east: Dayun and Tonggu, both bordering Linxiang County. To the southeast: Lingwu and Wulong. The Yangzi lay to the northwest; Dongting Lake to the southwest. Junshan, Bianshan, and Shicheng Mountain all stood in the lake. The lake measured over eight hundred li around, linked south to Qingcao and west to Chisha as the Three Lakes, where the Xiang, Yuan, Zi, and Li all converged. Northeast to Sanjiangkou it met the Yangzi at what antiquity called the Five Moors. The Yangzi then ran northeast into Linxiang. Chenglingji was a natural fortress. South ran the Xinqiang River—the Wei—which entered from Linxiang, flowed southwest, took Shagang Harbor on the left, wound west to Guankou, and entered Dongting Lake. It rose in the southeast at Qingshui Ridge, ran southwest to Xiangyin, and joined the Mi River. Man Lake lay southeast, also called Weng Lake; still farther east was Jiaozi Lake. At Yanglin Street an assistant magistrate was stationed. At Lujiao Market town a registrar was stationed. To the east: the Yueyang postal station. The Qinggang postal station, established in Shunzhi 16, had an assistant until Qianlong 16 abolished it. Linxiang was rated pivotal and busy. It lay ninety li northeast of the prefectural seat. To the east: Huanggao. To the southwest: Weiluo. To the southeast: Dayun. Also Mount Longjiao, spanning Tongcheng, Puqi, and other counties in Hubei—the Wei rose there, wound west past Tucheng, took Magang Harbor on the left, and entered Baling from the southwest. The Yangzi ran west of the county, entering from Baling and passing northeast by Pengcheng Mountain as Songyang Lake water poured in from the southeast. Farther northeast it met Baini Lake water, passed Yalanji, and entered Jiayu in Hubei. Huanggai Lake in the northeast received all waters east of the county, ran north to Qingjiangkou, and entered the Yangzi. Southeast stood the Taolin and Chang'an patrol offices; at Chenglingji, Qianlong 26 moved Chang'an Market town and renamed it, but the old name was soon restored. It had the Yunxi and Chang'an postal stations. Market towns at Yalanji and Chang'an. Huarong was rated exhausted and difficult. It lay one hundred eighty li northwest of the prefectural seat. To the north: Huanghu. To the east: Shimen and Moshan. To the northeast: Mount Dong. To the southeast: Mount Gulou. The Yangzi's right distributary entered from Jianli in Hubei, bent east and south into Baling. The Huarong River to the north and Yong River to the west both first took Yangzi water, entering from Shishou in Hubei and flowing southeast into Dongting Lake. South of the county the Li entered from Anxiang, merged with Chisha Lake, and also drained into Dongting. Dajing and Tuan lakes in the northeast joined and flowed into the Yangzi. It had the Huangjiaxue patrol office. Market towns at Huangjia and Gulou. Pingjiang was rated exhausted and difficult. It lay two hundred forty li southeast of the prefectural seat. To the north: Yongning. To the west: Huyuan. To the east: Daoyan. To the southeast: Lianyun. To the northeast: Mount Mufu, also called Mount Tianyue, with Tianyue Pass below it. Also the Mi River entered from Yining in Jiangxi, flowed southwest, took Hongqiao water on the right and the Baigian streams on the left, ran southwest to Baihukou, bent north, and received Zhongdong water flowing south then bending west. Still farther west it met the Lu River, northwest joined the Xianjiang River, bent southwest past the south of the county seat, and took Jinkeng water on the left. Still northwest to Jiangjun Mountain it met Changshan coming from the northeast, then wound west into Xiangyin. To the east stood the Changshou patrol office.
7
常德府：沖，繁，難。 隸岳常澧道。 舊隸湖廣布政使司，康熙三年來屬。 東南距省治四百十五里。 廣四百二十里，袤六百二十里。 北極高二十九度一分。 京師偏西五度十分。 領縣四。 商埠，光緒三十二年奏開。 武陵沖，繁，疲，難。 倚。 西有平山，即武陵山，亦名河洑。 北有陽山。 東北：藥山。 東南：善德山。 沅水自桃源入，南逕河洑洲，屈而東，至府治東南，歧為馬家吉河水。 又東南流，枉水自西南來注之。 又東過牛鼻灘，北別出為小河水，東北匯連山湖，合漸水。 沅水又東南入龍陽。 漸水在北，一名澹水，源出安福，南流屈東，右納馬家吉河水，又東北至馬家洲，歧為二，一東與小河水合，一東北合麻河水，至沙夾入沅水。 東北有衝天湖、直山湖、官塘湖，皆合漸水。 縣丞一，治牛鼻灘。 北有大龍巡司，乾隆四十一年置，後廢。 有麻河驛。 桃源沖，繁，難。 府西南八十里。 北：纛旗。 南：綠蘿。 西南：桃源。 沅水在南，自沅陵入，東過高都鎮，左納大洑溪，又東北與小洑溪合。 屈而東，夷望溪東流北屈注之。 又東合水溪，過縣治東南，屈而北，延溪水自西來入。 又東北與白洋河合。 河出慈利，曰龍潭河，東南入縣境，合蘭溪、湯溪，又南流為漆家河，入沅水，又東南入武陵。 新店、鄭家店二巡司。 又高都、鄭家店二廢巡司。 新店、鄭家店、桃源三驛。 蘇溪、麻溪、高都三鎮。 龍陽沖。 府東南八十里。 南：橫山，一名龍陽山，縣以此名。 北：寶台。 東南：軍山。 東北：洞庭湖。 沅水自武陵入，東過小河口，屈而南，滄浪水自西南來注之。 東過縣治東北，南別出為支港，東通後江湖，至沅江縣合資水。 其正渠又東北至鼎港口，小河水分流來注之。 又東北流為西河，漸水合小河水自西來會，入於洞庭。 其入湖處謂之西河口也。 東南有龍潭橋巡司。 龍陽驛。 小江、鼎口二鎮。 沅江簡。 府東南二百七十一里。 西南：煙波山，西北：赤山，東北：明山，並濱洞庭湖。 湖水西自龍陽受資水。 資水自益陽入，迤東至毛角子口，南別出為喬江水，至湘陰會湘水。 其正渠北屈而西，又西北過縣治東，白泥湖水首受益水，自西南來注之。 又北至小河口，歧為二，一東北流，至益陽江口入洞庭，一西北與沅水合，匯於洞庭湖。
Changde Prefecture was rated pivotal, busy, and difficult. It was subordinate to the Yuechangli Circuit. Formerly under the Huguang provincial administration commission, it came under Hunan in Kangxi 3. It lay four hundred fifteen li southeast of the provincial seat. It measured four hundred twenty li east to west and six hundred twenty li north to south. North polar altitude was 29°1′. Longitude was 5°10′ west of the capital. It governed four counties. A treaty port was opened by memorial in Guangxu 32. Wuling was rated pivotal, busy, exhausted, and difficult. Attached to the prefectural seat. To the west: Mount Pingshan—that is, Mount Wuling, also called Hebo. To the north: Mount Yang. To the northeast: Mount Yao. To the southeast: Mount Shande. The Yuan entered from Taoyuan, passed south by Hebo Isle, bent east to the southeast of the prefectural seat, and split as the Majiaji River. It ran farther southeast as the Wang River poured in from the southwest. Farther east it passed Niubi Shoal; a northern branch became the Xiao River, which northeast gathered Lianshan Lake and joined the Jian River. The Yuan then ran southeast into Longyang. North ran the Jian River, also called the Dan River, rising in Anfu, flowing south then bending east, taking Majiaji River water on the right, then northeast to Majia Isle where it split: one branch east joined the Xiao River, one northeast joined the Ma River, both reaching Shajia to enter the Yuan. Northeast, Chongtian, Zhishan, and Guantang lakes all fed the Jian River. One assistant magistrate was stationed at Niubi Shoal. To the north stood the Dalong patrol office, established in Qianlong 41, later abolished. It had the Mahe postal station. Taoyuan was rated pivotal, busy, and difficult. It lay eighty li southwest of the prefectural seat. To the north: Daoji. To the south: Lüluo. To the southwest: Taoyuan. The Yuan lay south of the county, entering from Yuanling, passing east by Gaodu Market town, taking Dafu Stream on the left, then northeast joining Xiaofu Stream. It bent east as Yiwang Stream flowed east then bent north to pour in. Farther east it joined Shui Stream, passed southeast of the county seat, bent north, and Yanshi Stream entered from the west. Farther northeast it joined the Baiyang River. Rising in Cili as Longtan River, it entered the county southeast, joined Lan and Tang streams, flowed south as the Qijia River into the Yuan, then southeast into Wuling. It had the Xindian and Zhengjiadian patrol offices. Also the abolished patrol offices of Gaodu and Zhengjiadian. It had the Xindian, Zhengjiadian, and Taoyuan postal stations. Market towns at Suxi, Maxi, and Gaodu. Longyang was rated pivotal. It lay eighty li southeast of the prefectural seat. To the south: Heng Mountain, also called Longyang Mountain, for which the county was named. To the north: Baotai. To the southeast: Jun Mountain. To the northeast: Dongting Lake. The Yuan entered from Wuling, passed east by Xiaokou Harbor, bent south, and the Canglang River poured in from the southwest. It ran east past the northeast of the county seat, split south as a side channel, reached east to Houjiang Lake, and at Yuanjiang County met the Zi River. The main channel ran farther northeast to Dinggang Harbor as Xiao River water branched in. It ran farther northeast as the West River, where the Jian and Xiao rivers met from the west and entered Dongting. Its lake entry was called West River Mouth. Southeast stood the Longtan Bridge patrol office. It had the Longyang postal station. Market towns at Xiaojiang and Dingkou. Yuanjiang County was rated simple. It lay two hundred seventy-one li southeast of the prefectural seat. Southwest: Yanbo Mountain; northwest: Chi Mountain; northeast: Ming Mountain—all along Dongting Lake. Westward, the lake took the Zi River at Longyang. The Zi entered from Yiyang, wound east to Maojiaozi Mouth, split south as the Qiao River, and at Xiangyin met the Xiang. Its main channel bent north and west, passed northwest east of the county seat, and Baini Lake water—fed first by the Zi—poured in from the southwest. Farther north at Xiaokou Harbor it split: one branch northeast to the Yiyang River mouth into Dongting, one northwest to join the Yuan in Dongting Lake.
8
澧州直隸州：沖，繁，難。 岳常澧道駐。 舊為岳屬州，雍正七年升，割石門、安鄉、慈利來隸，並置安福。 十三年增永定。 東南距省治六百有五里。 廣四百三十五里，袤二百有五里。 北極高二十九度三十七分。 京師偏西四度四十四分。 領縣五。 西北：天供、大清。 東南：關山、彭山、銅山、大浮。 澧水在南，自安福入，東北流，東別出為內河，屈東南至道口，道水自西南來注之。 又東至六冢口合澹水。 水出石門東，過州治北，屈而南，又東至伍公嘴，涔水自西北來會。 又南合澧水，至匯口入於安鄉。 東有虎渡水，一名後小江，首受大江水，自湖北公安入，南流為一箭河水，其左岸則安鄉縣界也。 又南至匯口入澧水。 州判駐津市鎮。 清化、順林二巡司。 蘭松水、馬二驛。 匯口、三汊河、津市、嘉山四鎮。 順林司。 後廢。 石門難。 州西南九十里。 雍正七年自岳州來屬。 西：石門。 北：燕子。 西北：層步，一名層山。 又西北有盧黃山。 澧水在南，又曰零陽河，自慈利入，北屈而東，與渫水合。 水出西北龍門洞，東南流，右納黃水，左納溫水，又東南至渫口入澧水。 澧水又東過縣治南，雙溪水自北來注之。 又東北合朝陽溪水，入安福。 又道水自慈利入，亦東北流入安福。 西北有水南渡巡司。 安鄉簡。 州東南一百二十里。 雍正七年自岳州來屬。 北：黃山。 東：石家。 西：石龜。 西北：古田。 澧水在西，自州入，南至匯口，西別出為羌口河。 又西南流為麻河，至武陵入漸水。 其正渠東南匯於大鯨湖。 又東過縣治南，長河水首受大江，北自公安來注之。 又東南入南洲。 又東，後江水，亦受大江，自湖北石首入，南流為景港水，至南洲入澧水。 大溶湖北受澧水，注於沅。 康熙十八年置焦圻、南平二驛，後廢。 有羌口鎮。 慈利簡。 州西南一百六十里。 雍正七年自岳州來屬。 北：道人。 東北：星子。 西南：零陽。 又有雲朝山。 澧水在西，自永定入，東至褚溪口，右合九渡水，又東北與九谿河水合。 水出湖北鶴峰州，即古漊水也。 又東過縣治北，右納零溪水。 入石門。 又道水亦東北入石門。 又龍潭河出西南，南至桃源入沅水。 澧水在境為洲渚者八，為潭者二，為灘瀨者百三十二。 有麻寮所、九谿衛城巡司。 安福難。 州西南六十里。 雍正七年以慈利縣九谿衛地置，析澧州地益之，治裴家河，來屬。 北：大銅。 東：營駐。 西南：大浮山，山跨石門、桃源、武陵諸縣。 澧水在北。 自石門入，迤東流，左納合溪，右納惡蛇溪，又東入澧州。 又道水在縣南，亦自石門入，東北至澧州入澧水。 有添平所、新安市巡司，乾隆三十二年廢。 永定疲，難。 州西南三百四十里。 雍正十三年以慈利永定衛置，析安福縣地益之，治舊衛城，來屬。 南：天門。 西南：崇山。 西北：馬耳。 東北：香爐。 澧水在南，自桑植入，南屈而東，武溪水自南來注之，又東與大庸溪合。 又東流，左納無事溪，右納仙人溪，又過縣治東南，西溪水北流入焉，又東合社溪入慈利。 又九渡水出縣南，東北至慈利入澧水。 大庸所城在縣西。
Li Direct-Controlled Prefecture was rated pivotal, busy, and difficult. The Yuechangli Circuit was stationed there. Formerly a prefecture subordinate to Yuezhou, it was promoted in Yongzheng 7; Shimen, Anxiang, and Cili were transferred to it, and Anfu was established. In Yongzheng 13 Yongding was added. It lay six hundred five li southeast of the provincial seat. It measured four hundred thirty-five li east to west and two hundred five li north to south. North polar altitude was 29°37′. Longitude was 4°44′ west of the capital. It governed five counties. To the northwest: Tiangong and Daqing. To the southeast: Guanshan, Pengshan, Tongshan, and Dafu. The Li lay south, entering from Anfu and flowing northeast; an eastern branch became the Inner River, bent southeast to Daokou, and the Dao River poured in from the southwest. Farther east at Liuzhong Mouth it joined the Dan River. It rose east of Shimen, passed north of the prefectural seat, bent south, ran east to Wugong Mouth, and met the Cen River from the northwest. Farther south it joined the Li and at Huikou entered Anxiang. East ran the Hudu River, also called the Houxiao—it first took the Yangzi from Gong'an in Hubei, flowed south as the Yijian River, with Anxiang County on its left bank. Farther south at Huikou it entered the Li River. The prefectural judge was stationed at Jinshi Market town. It had the Qinghua and Shunlin patrol offices. Postal stations at Lansongshui and Ma'er. Market towns at Huikou, Sach River, Jinshi, and Jiashan. The Shunlin patrol office. It was later abolished. Shimen County was rated difficult. It lay ninety li southwest of the prefectural seat. In Yongzheng 7 it was transferred from Yuezhou to Li Prefecture. To the west: Shimen. To the north: Yanzi. To the northwest: Cengbu, also called Ceng Mountain. Farther northwest stood Luhuang Mountain. South ran the Li River, also called Lingyang River, entering from Cili, bending north and east to join the Xie River. It rose at Longmen Cave in the northwest, ran southeast taking Huang River water on the right and Wen River water on the left, then southeast to Xiekou to enter the Li. The Li ran farther east past the south of the county seat as Shuangxi River poured in from the north. Farther northeast it joined Chaoyang Stream and entered Anfu. The Dao River also entered from Cili and ran northeast into Anfu. Northwest stood the Shuinandu patrol office. Anxiang County was rated simple. It lay one hundred twenty li southeast of the prefectural seat. In Yongzheng 7 it was transferred from Yuezhou to Li Prefecture. To the north: Huang Mountain. To the east: Shijia. To the west: Shigui. To the northwest: Gutian. The Li lay west, entering from the prefectural seat; south to Huikou a western branch became the Qiangkou River. Farther southwest it ran as the Ma River into the Jian at Wuling. Its main channel gathered southeast in Dajing Lake. Farther east it passed south of the county seat as Chang River water—first taking the Yangzi from Gong'an to the north—poured in. Farther southeast it entered Nanzhou. Farther east, the Hou River also took the Yangzi from Shishou in Hubei, flowed south as the Jinggang River, and at Nanzhou entered the Li. Darong Lake took the Li from the north and fed the Yuan. The Jiaoqi and Nanping postal stations, established in Kangxi 18, were later abolished. It had Qiangkou Market town. Cili County was rated simple. It lay one hundred sixty li southwest of the prefectural seat. In Yongzheng 7 it was transferred from Yuezhou to Li Prefecture. To the north: Daoren. To the northeast: Xingzi. To the southwest: Lingyang. Yunchao Mountain also stood there. The Li lay west, entering from Yongding, running east to Chuxikou with Jiudu River water on the right, then northeast joining Jiuxi River water. It rose in Hefeng Prefecture, Hubei—the ancient Li River. Farther east it passed north of the county seat, taking Ling Stream water on the right. It entered Shimen. The Dao River also ran northeast into Shimen. Longtan River also rose in the southwest and ran south to Taoyuan to enter the Yuan. Within the county the Li formed eight islets, two pools, and one hundred thirty-two rapids. It had the Maliang guard station and the Jiuxi guard-town patrol office. Anfu County was rated difficult. It lay sixty li southwest of the prefectural seat. In Yongzheng 7 it was created on Jiuxi guard territory in Cili, with Li Prefecture land added, seat at Peijia River, and placed under Li Prefecture. To the north: Datong. To the east: Yingzhu. To the southwest: Dafu Mountain, spanning Shimen, Taoyuan, Wuling, and other counties. The Li lay north. It entered from Shimen, wound east, took He Stream on the left and Eshe Stream on the right, and ran east into Li Prefecture. The Dao River also lay south of the county, entering from Shimen and running northeast into the Li at Li Prefecture. It had the Tianping guard station and Xinshi Market patrol office, abolished in Qianlong 32. Yongding was rated exhausted and difficult. It lay three hundred forty li southwest of the prefectural seat. In Yongzheng 13 it was created from Yongding guard territory in Cili, with Anfu County land added, seat at the old guard town, and placed under Li Prefecture. To the south: Tianmen. To the southwest: Chongshan. To the northwest: Ma'er. To the northeast: Xianglu. The Li lay south, entering from Sangzhi, bending south then east as Wu River water joined from the south, then east meeting Dayong Stream. Still flowing east, it took Wushi Stream on the left and Xianren Stream on the right, passed southeast of the seat as Xixi River entered from the north, then east joined She Stream and entered Cili. Jiudu River also rose south of the county and ran northeast into the Li at Cili. The Dayong guard town lay west of the county.
9
南州直隸廳：繁，疲，難。 隸岳常澧道。 本華容縣地，咸豐四年，湖北石首縣藕池口決，江水溢入洞庭，淤為洲。 光緒十七年置廳，治九都市，並析華容、巴陵、安鄉、武陵、龍陽、沅江諸縣地益之。 東南距省治五百四十里。 廣一百一十里，袤九十里。 北極高二十九度二十一分。 京師偏西四度一十三分。 北：太陽山。 東：明山。 西南：清介。 東南：洞庭湖。 寄山、團山皆在湖中。 西有澧水自安鄉入，東南逕白板口，歧為二，一西南至天心湖合沅水，一東與後江水合，又西南至冷飯洲，匯於洞庭。 又有游橋水，首受後江，南至麻濠口入洞庭。 又涌水自華容入，東南流，至廳治東北，南別出為神童港，與游橋水會。 迤東過明山，其北岸則華容縣界也，又東至鋸子口入洞庭湖。
Nanzhou Direct-Control Department was rated busy, exhausted, and difficult. It was subordinate to the Yuechangli Circuit. It was originally Huarong County land. In Xianfeng 4 the breach at Ouchi Mouth in Shishou, Hubei, sent the Yangtze flooding into Dongting and silted up as islets. In Guangxu 17 the department was established with seat at Jiudu Market, adding land partitioned from Huarong, Baling, Anxiang, Wuling, Longyang, Yuanjiang, and other counties. It lay five hundred forty li southeast of the provincial seat. It measured one hundred ten li across and ninety li long. Latitude was 29°21′ N. Longitude was 4°13′ west of the capital. To the north: Taiyang Mountain. To the east: Ming Mountain. To the southwest: Qingjie. To the southeast: Dongting Lake. Jishan and Tuanshan both lay in the lake. West, the Li entered from Anxiang, wound southeast past Baibankou, split in two—one branch southwest to Tianxin Lake to meet the Yuan, one east joined Houjiang River—then southwest to Lengfan Isle and into Dongting. Also Youqiao River, taking Houjiang first, ran south to Mahekou to enter Dongting. Also Yong River entered from Huarong, flowed southeast to northeast of the seat, split south as Shentong Harbor, and met Youqiao River. It wound east past Ming Mountain with Huarong County on the north bank, then east to Juzi Mouth to enter Dongting Lake.
10
衡州府：沖，繁，難。 隸衡永郴桂道。 舊隸湖廣布政使司。 康熙三年來屬。 乾隆中增置清泉。 東北距省治三百八十里。 廣四百六十里，袤二百九十五里。 北極高二十六度五十六分。 京師偏西四度五分。 領縣七。 衡陽沖，繁，疲，難。 倚。 城內金鼇山。 北：岣嶁山。 西北：九峰、黃龍。 西南：大雲山。 東南：湘水左瀆自清泉入，北過府治東，北受烝水。 水出邵陽東，合等江水，至陡江口，岳山水南流入焉。 右納演陂，南流，武水自西南來會，納清化河，其右岸則清泉縣界也。 東北逕石鼓山入湘水。 又北，東入于衡山。 有寒溪鎮。 縣丞治查江市。 有衡陽驛。 清泉疲，難。 倚。 乾隆二十一年析衡陽縣東南鄉置，來屬。 東：清泉山，縣以此名。 南：回雁峰，衡岳之首峰也。 南：雨母。 西南：七寶、探山。 湘水自祁陽入，迤東流，右界常寧縣，栗江水自西北來注之。 又東過茭河口，西北過府治東。 合耒水。 北屈而東入衡山。 西南：柿江水、清化水，皆東北至衡陽入烝水。 東南有新城市巡司。 廖田驛。 衡山沖，繁，難。 府東北一百里。 西北：衡山，是為南嶽。 東：靈山。 東北：鳳凰。 東南：楊山，又名武陽山。 湘水自衡陽入，東北合龍隱港水，至茶陵江口，洣水合永樂江自東南來注之。 北過縣治東，為觀湘洲。 右納石灣港，左納樊田港，又北，東入湘潭。 又涓水源出湘鄉，東合興樂江，東北至湘潭入湘水。 有草市、永壽二巡司。 雷家鎮有驛。 耒陽沖，繁，難。 府東南一百五十里。 西：石臼。 東：侯計山，跨安仁、永興二縣。 東南：天門。 東北：明月。 耒水自永興入，東北流，右納肥江，西北至城南，屈東北，潯江水自東來注之，西北入清泉。 其東馬水從之，亦至清泉入耒水。 羅渡鎮有廢巡司。 有驛。 常寧難。 府西南一百二十里。 北：憩山。 西南：塔山、液麻山。 東南有逍遙。 東北：盟山。 西北：湘水右瀆自祁陽入，合吳水。 又東北，左與清泉分岸。 又東與宜水合。 水出縣南西江山，北逕縣治西，左有藍江，右有潭水，皆流合焉，又東北至江口市入湘水。 湘水又東北流，右納鹽湖，至茭河口，舂水北流西屈來會。 水自桂陽州入，一名茭源河，其東岸則耒陽縣界也。 湘水又北入清泉。 有杉樹堡。 西南壤接瑤峒。 安仁簡。 府東南一百五十里。 南：大湖山。 西：金紫。 北：軍山。 東北：排山。 東南：大松山。 西北：永樂江自永興入，北與浦陽港合。 又北流，左納油陂港，右納蓮花港，北至安平市，大坪港西流合焉。 又過城西北，宜陽港水自南來注之，西北至衡山入洣水。 有潭湖鎮、安平鎮廢巡司。 酃簡。 府東南三百里。 北：青台。 南：泰和。 東南：萬陽。 西南：屏水山。 山與桂東接界，洣水出焉。 迤北至雙江口，漠渡水北流西屈注之。 又西合春江，即雲秋水，東北合洣水入茶陵，是為茶陵江。 其東沔渡水，北為洮水，下流合於洣水。
Hengzhou Prefecture was rated pivotal, busy, and difficult. It was subordinate to the Heng-Yong-Chen-Gui Circuit. Formerly under the Huguang provincial administration commission. In Kangxi 3 it came under Hunan. During the Qianlong reign Qingquan County was added. It lay three hundred eighty li northeast of the provincial seat. It measured four hundred sixty li across and two hundred ninety-five li long. Latitude was 26°56′ N. Longitude was 4°5′ west of the capital. It governed seven counties. Hengyang was rated pivotal, busy, exhausted, and difficult. Attached to the prefectural seat. Within the city stood Jinao Mountain. To the north: Mount Gouluo. To the northwest: Jiufeng and Huanglong. To the southwest: Dayun Mountain. Southeast, the Xiang's left distributary entered from Qingquan, passed north by the east of the prefectural seat, and took the Zheng River from the north. It rose east of Shaoyang, united with Deng River water, and at Doujiang Mouth Yue Mountain water joined from the south. It took Yanbei on the right, flowed south, met the Wu River from the southwest and Qinghua River, with Qingquan County on the right bank. It passed northeast by Shigu Mountain to enter the Xiang. Farther north it ran east into Hengshan County. It had Hanxi Market town. The assistant magistrate was stationed at Chajiang Market. It had the Hengyang postal station. Qingquan was rated exhausted and difficult. Attached to the prefectural seat. In Qianlong 21 the southeastern township of Hengyang was partitioned to create it, and it was placed under Hengzhou Prefecture. East lay Qingquan Mountain, for which the county was named. South stood Huiyan Peak, the foremost peak of Mount Heng. To the south: Yumu. To the southwest: Qibao and Tanshan. The Xiang entered from Qiyang, wound east with Changning County on the right, and Lijiang River joined from the northwest. It ran farther east past Jiaokou and northwest past the east of the prefectural seat. It joined the Lei River. It bent north then east into Hengshan County. Southwest, Shijiang River and Qinghua River both ran northeast to Hengyang to enter the Zheng River. Southeast stood the Xincheng Market patrol office. It had the Liaotian postal station. Hengshan County was rated pivotal, busy, and difficult. It lay one hundred li northeast of the prefectural seat. To the northwest: Mount Heng—the Southern Sacred Peak. To the east: Ling Mountain. To the northeast: Fenghuang. To the southeast: Yang Mountain, also called Wuyang Mountain. The Xiang entered from Hengyang, northeast took Longyin Harbor water, and at Chaling River mouth Mi River united with Yongle River from the southeast. North of the seat it formed Guanxiang Isle. It took Shiwan Harbor on the right and Fantian Harbor on the left, then north and east into Xiangtan. Also Juan River rose in Xiangxiang, east joined Xingle River, and northeast to Xiangtan entered the Xiang. It had the Caoshi and Yongshou patrol offices. Leijia Market town had a postal station. Leiyang was rated pivotal, busy, and difficult. It lay one hundred fifty li southeast of the prefectural seat. To the west: Shijiu. To the east: Houji Mountain, spanning Anren and Yongxing counties. To the southeast: Tianmen. To the northeast: Mingyue. The Lei entered from Yongxing, flowed northeast, took Fei River on the right, northwest to south of the city, bent northeast as Xun River joined from the east, and northwest into Qingquan. East of it Ma River likewise reached Qingquan to enter the Lei. Luodu Market town had an abolished patrol office. It had a postal station. Changning was rated difficult. It lay one hundred twenty li southwest of the prefectural seat. To the north: Qishan. To the southwest: Tashan and Yema Mountain. To the southeast: Xiaoyao. To the northeast: Meng Mountain. Northwest, the Xiang's right distributary entered from Qiyang and joined Wu River. Farther northeast it shared the bank with Qingquan on the left. Farther east it met Yi River. It rose south of the county at Xijiang Mountain, north past west of the seat with Lan River on the left and Tan River on the right, united, then northeast to Jiangkou Market to enter the Xiang. The Xiang flowed northeast again, took Yan Lake on the right, and at Jiaokou Chong River flowing north then bending west came to meet it. It entered from Guiyang Prefecture, also called Jiaoyuan River, with Leiyang County on the east bank. The Xiang ran north again into Qingquan. It had Shanshu Fort. To the southwest its soil bordered Yao dong territory. Anren County was rated simple. It lay one hundred fifty li southeast of the prefectural seat. To the south: Dahu Mountain. To the west: Jinzi. To the north: Jun Mountain. To the northeast: Paishan. To the southeast: Dasong Mountain. Northwest, Yongle River entered from Yongxing and north joined Puyang Harbor. It flowed north again, took Youbei Harbor on the left and Lianhua Harbor on the right, reached Anping Market, and Daping Harbor flowing west joined it. Farther northwest of the city Yiyang Harbor water joined from the south, then northwest to Hengshan County to enter the Mi River. It had Tanhu and Anping market towns with abolished patrol offices. Ling County was rated simple. It lay three hundred li southeast of the prefectural seat. To the north: Qingtai. To the south: Taihe. To the southeast: Wanyang. To the southwest: Pingshui Mountain. The mountain bordered Guidong, and the Mi River rose there. It wound north to Shuangjiang Mouth, where Modu River flowing north then bending west joined it. Farther west it met Chun River, namely Yunqiu River, and northeast united with the Mi to enter Chaling as the Chaling River. East of it lay Miandu River; to the north Tao River flowed down to join the Mi.
11
永州府：沖，繁。 隸辰沅永靖道。 總兵駐。 舊屬湖廣布政使司。 康熙三年來屬。 北距省治六百七十里。 廣三百四十里。 袤五百九十里。 北極高二十六度九分。 京師偏西四度五十三分。 領州一，縣七。 江藍同知一，嘉慶十九年移治江華縣濤墟市，後又遷於錦田所城。 通判一，道光十二年移治新田縣楊家鋪。 零陵沖，繁，難。 倚。 城內萬石山。 西：西山。 北：萬石。 東北：巋山。 東南：陽明山。 西南：石城山、永山。 湘水自東安合西南石頭江入，至府治西北，東南瀟水自道州合麻江水入，北與永水逕袁家渡至城南，合愚溪及鈷鉧潭來會，是為瀟湘。 湘水北與蘆洪江水合，又北，東入祁陽。 黃溪水出東南，馬子江出西南，併流合湘水。 縣丞駐泠水灘。 北有黃楊堡巡司，後廢。 有驛。 祁陽沖，繁。 府東北一百里。 北有祁山，縣以是名。 南：白水。 東南：樂山。 東北：七星，即大雲山。 西北：四望山。 湘水自零陵入，東納浯溪，過縣城南，合祁水。 水一名小東江，古曰𣲭口，源出西北騰雲嶺，東南流，煙江水自北來會，入湘水。 湘水迤東過白水鎮，白江水合黃溪水自西南來注之。 屈東北，與清江水合。 水出縣北鎮潭山，即古餘溪水也。 東有歸陽市巡司，乾隆二十一年移治排山驛，尋復故。 文明市有永隆廢巡司。 有驛。 有白水、樂山、文明、沙鎮、大營五鎮。 東安簡。 府西九十里。 北：東山。 西北：舜峰。 東北：高霞。 東南：伏虎。 湘水自廣西全州流入，北屈而東，清溪江合宥江水自西北來注之，東與石期江水合，又東北入零陵。 蘆洪江源出東北八十四渡山，東南流，左會龍合江，東南至零陵入湘水。 有蘆洪市巡司，石期市廢司。 淥埠、石期、荊塘三鎮道州難。 府南一百五十里。 城內元山。 北：宜山。 西北：瀟山、營道山。 西南：營山。 又都龐嶺界接永明，蓋五嶺之第三嶺也。 瀟水在東。 即古營水，又曰泥江，自寧遠縣入，西北至青口，與南源沱水合。 水自江華入，北屈而西，合掩水，東北至州治南，營道水自西南來注之，今謂之小營水。 又東北，左納宜江，會瀟水。 其會流處曰三江口。 瀟水又北納麻江水，入零陵。 有白灘營。 永安關界廣西灌陽。 瑤山在東南。 寧遠簡。 府東南一百八十里。 南：九疑山，跨道州、江華、藍山諸縣。 北：陽明山、黃溪山。 東北：舂陵，一名仰山。 瀟水在南，源出九疑三分石，西北至江口會瀑水。 水出東南舜源峰，即古泠水也，北流合漭水。 又西北過縣治，都溪水自東北來注之，入瀟水。 東北白江水，北入祁陽。 其西大竹源水，一名楊柳溪，亦東北至祁陽。 有梅岡鎮。 九疑魯觀巡司。 永明難。 府西南二百二十里。 北：永明嶺。 即都龐嶺。 東南：馬山。 西南：荊峽鎮山，其下有鎮峽關，界接廣西恭城縣。 掩水源出西北大掩峰，北過縣治西，右合古澤水，屈而東，角馬河水自東南來注之，東北至道州會沱水。 西南沐水，南合遨水，西至桃川所城，右納皋澤，左納扶靈，西南入於恭城，其下流是為平樂水也。 西南周棠寨巡司。 又有白面墟司巡檢，後遷東南枇杷所城，更名，尋廢。 桃川廢司。 白象鎮。 瑤山在縣西。 江華繁。 府南二百二十里。 東：豸山。 南：吳望。 西南：蒼梧嶺，即臨賀嶺，又名萌渚嶺，跨廣西富川、賀縣，蓋五嶺之第四嶺也。 沱水在東，上源曰中河，自藍山入，南屈而東，前河、後河皆流合焉，又西南逕錦田所城。 宜遷水出廣東連山，西北流注之，西與靈江合。 又西北合馮水，今謂之練江水也，至縣城東曰東河。 西河曰萌渚水，自西南來會，又西北入道州。 西南有錦岡巡司、錦田廢司。 瑤山在縣東。 新田簡。 府東南二百八十里。 南：七賢、藍山。 西北：舂陵山，與桂陽州寧遠縣接界。 舂水出焉，俗曰烏江水，東南逕夫人山，又南至縣城西南為西河水，東河水自東北來注之，又東屈而北，入於桂陽。 東南白面墟廢司。 東有瑤山。
Yongzhou Prefecture was rated pivotal and busy. It was subordinate to the Chen-Yuan-Yongjing Circuit. A regional commander was stationed there. Formerly it was under the Huguang provincial administration commission. In Kangxi 3 it came under Hunan. It lay six hundred seventy li north of the provincial capital. It measured three hundred forty li east to west. It measured five hundred ninety li north to south. Latitude was 26°9′ N. Longitude was 4°53′ west of the capital. It governed one subordinate prefecture and seven counties. It had one Jianghua-Lan associate prefect; in Jiaqing 19 the seat moved to Taoxu Market in Jianghua County and later to Jintian guard city. It had one intendant; in Daoguang 12 the seat moved to Yangjia Market in Xintian County. Lingling County was rated pivotal, busy, and difficult. Attached to the prefectural seat. Within the city stood Wanshi Mountain. To the west: Xishan. To the north: Wanshi. To the northeast: Kuishan. To the southeast: Yangming Mountain. To the southwest: Shicheng Mountain and Yong Mountain. The Xiang entered from Dong'an with Shitou River from the southwest to the northwest of the seat; the Xiao entered from Daozhou with Majiang River from the southeast; Yong River ran north by Yuanjia Ford to the south of the city and met Yuxi and Gumu Pool—forming the Xiaoxiang confluence. The Xiang ran north to meet Luhong River water, then north and east into Qiyang County. Huangxi River rose in the southeast and Mazi River in the southwest; they united and entered the Xiang. The assistant magistrate was stationed at Lingshui Beach. To the north stood Huangyang Fort patrol office, later abolished. It had a postal station. Qiyang County was rated pivotal and busy. It lay one hundred li northeast of the prefectural seat. To the north stood Mount Qi, for which the county was named. To the south: Baishui. To the southeast: Leshan. To the northeast: Qixing, namely Dayun Mountain. To the northwest: Siwang Mountain. The Xiang entered from Lingling, took Wuxi on the east, passed south of the seat, and joined the Qi River. Also called Little East River and anciently Xikou, it rose at Tengyun Ridge in the northwest, flowed southeast, met Yan River from the north, and entered the Xiang. The Xiang wound east past Baishui Market town as Baishui River united with Huangxi River from the southwest. It bent northeast and met Qing River. It rose at Zhentan Mountain north of the county—the ancient Yuxi River. East stood Guiyang Market patrol office; in Qianlong 21 it moved to Paishan postal station, soon restored. Wenming Market town had an abolished patrol office. It had a postal station. It had the market towns of Baishui, Leshan, Wenming, Shazhen, and Daying. Dong'an County was rated simple. It lay ninety li west of the prefectural seat. To the north: Dongshan. To the northwest: Shunfeng. To the northeast: Gaoxia. To the southeast: Fuhu. The Xiang entered from Quanzhou in Guangxi, bent north then east, took Qingxi united with You River from the northwest, met Shiji River on the east, and ran northeast into Lingling. Luhong River rose at Bashisidu Mountain in the northeast, flowed southeast, took Longhe River on the left, and southeast to Lingling entered the Xiang. It had Luhong Market patrol office; Shiji Market town had an abolished office. It had the market towns of Lubu, Shiji, and Jingtang. Daozhou was rated difficult. It lay one hundred fifty li south of the prefectural seat. Within the city stood Yuan Mountain. To the north: Yishan. To the northwest: Xiaoshan and Yingdao Mountain. To the southwest: Yingshan. Dupang Ridge also bordered Yongming—the third of the Five Ridges. The Xiao River lay to the east. It was the ancient Ying River, also called Ni River, entering from Ningyuan County northwest to Qingkou to meet the southern-source Tuojiang. It entered from Jianghua, bent north then west, joined Yanshui, ran northeast to south of the seat as Yingdao River joined from the southwest—now called Little Ying River. Farther northeast it took Yijiang on the left and met the Xiao River. Their confluence was called Sanjiang Mouth. The Xiao ran north again, took Majiang River, and entered Lingling. It had Baiban Garrison. Yong'an Pass bordered Guanyang in Guangxi. Yao Mountain stood in the southeast. Ningyuan County was rated simple. It lay one hundred eighty li southeast of the prefectural seat. To the south: Jiuyi Mountain, spanning Daozhou, Jianghua, and Lanshan counties. To the north: Yangming Mountain and Huangxi Mountain. To the northeast: Chunling, also called Yang Mountain. The Xiao lay south, rising at Sanfen Stone on Jiuyi, northwest to Jiangkou to meet Pao River. It rose at Shunyuan Peak in the southeast—the ancient Ling River—and flowed north to join Mang River. Farther northwest it passed the seat as Duxi River joined from the northeast to enter the Xiao. Northeast, Baishui River flowed north into Qiyang County. West of the county, the Dashuyuan River—also Yangliu Stream—also ran northeast into Qiyang. It had Meigang Market town. It had the Jiuyi Luguan patrol office. Yongming County was rated difficult. It lay two hundred twenty li southwest of the prefectural seat. To the north: Yongming Ridge. This was Dupang Ridge. To the southeast: Mashi. Southwest: Jingxia Market Mountain; below stood Zhenxia Pass, bordering Gongcheng County in Guangxi. Yanshui rose from Great Yan Peak in the northwest, passed north past the west of the seat, joined Guze on the right, bent east as Jiaoma River joined from the southeast, and ran northeast to Daozhou to meet Tuojiang. Southwest, Mu River joined Ao to the south, ran west to Taochuan guard city, took Gaozhe on the right and Fuling on the left, entered Gongcheng in the southwest—its lower course was Pingle River. Southwest stood the Zhoutang Stockade patrol office. Also the Baimian Market guard patrol inspectorate was later moved to Pipao guard city in the southeast, renamed, and soon abolished. The abolished Taochuan office. It had Baixiang Market town. Yao Mountain stood west of the county. Jianghua County was rated busy. It lay two hundred twenty li south of the prefectural seat. To the east: Zhishan. To the south: Wuwang. Southwest: Cangwu Ridge—the Linhe Ridge, also Mengzhu Ridge—spanning Fuchuan and He counties in Guangxi: the fourth of the Five Ridges. Tuojiang lay east; its upper stream was the Central River, entering from Lanshan, bending south then east as Front and Rear rivers united, then southwest past Jintian guard city. Yiqian rose in Lianshan, Guangdong, flowed northwest to join it, and west met Ling River. Farther northwest it met Feng River—now Lian River—east of the seat as the East River. The West River was Mengzhu River, joining from the southwest and running northwest into Daozhou. Southwest had the Jingang patrol office and the abolished Jintian office. Yao Mountain stood east of the county. Xintian County was rated simple. It lay two hundred eighty li southeast of the prefectural seat. To the south: Qixian and Lanshan. Northwest: Chunling Mountain, bordering Ningyuan County in Guiyang Prefecture. Chun River rose there—the popular Wujiang—ran southeast past Furen Mountain, south to southwest of the seat as the West River; the East River joined from the northeast, bent east then north into Guiyang. Southeast lay the abolished Baimian Market office. East stood Yao Mountain.
12
桂陽直隸州：繁，疲，難。 隸衡永郴桂道。 舊桂陽州隸衡州府。 雍正十年升為直隸府，仍所領。 東北距省治六百三十里。 廣二百二十七里，袤二百五十里。 北極高二十五度四十九分。 京師偏西四度零五分。 領縣三。 東：鹿峰。 西：大湊，一名寶山。 西北：壇山。 西南：石門。 東南：神渡。 舂水自新田入，北過象鼻嘴，漼水合鼠峽水自西北來注之，即桂水也。 屈東會鍾水，納泮溪，又北與楓江水合，至常寧入湘水。 東南：仰天湖，屯湖水出，西北流，左合麻淪江，又北與泉田水合。 屈東北，蓮蓬溪水北流來會，又東北入郴州。 南牛橋鎮、北泗州寨二廢巡司。 臨武簡。 州西南一百四十里。 北：八源，一名東山。 西：舜峰。 西南：華陰。 又有西山，古名桐柏山，溱水出焉，東北流，左納貝溪，與秀溪水合。 屈而北，武溪水合石江水自西來會。 又東，赤土溪水南流合焉，東南入宜章。 有赤土鎮。 瑤山在縣南。 藍山簡。 州西南一百五十里。 北：藍山。 西：九疑。 南：南風坳，界接廣東連州，鍾水出焉，西流屈北會巋水。 水出九疑山，曰九疑水，亦謂之舜水，東北逕縣治南，左納濛溪，屈而東，毛俊水合華荊津水自東南來注之，又北與藍溪水合，東北入嘉禾。 西南中河，入江華為沱水，下流合於瀟水。 有毛俊鎮。 大橋鎮巡司，後遷臨武營，更名。 瑤山在縣南。 嘉禾簡。 州西南一百一十里。 西：晉嶺，即藍山。 北：石門。 西北：石燕山。 鍾水在南，自藍山入，東北流，至縣城東北，含溪水自西來注之，北至桂陽州入舂水。 東南泮溪水，源出臨武，北與芹溪水合，亦至桂陽州入舂水。 有兩路口廢巡司。
Guiyang Direct-Controlled Prefecture was rated busy, exhausted, and difficult. It was subordinate to the Heng-Yong-Chen-Gui Circuit. Formerly Guiyang Prefecture was subordinate to Hengzhou Prefecture. In Yongzheng 10 it was raised to a direct-controlled prefecture while retaining its former jurisdictions. It lay six hundred thirty li northeast of the provincial seat. It measured two hundred twenty-seven li east to west and two hundred fifty li north to south. Latitude was 25°49′ N. Longitude was 4°5′ west of the capital. It governed three counties. To the east: Lufeng. To the west: Dacou, also called Baoshan. Northwest: Tanshan. Southwest: Shimen. Southeast: Shendu. Chun River entered from Xintian, passed north of Xiangbizui as Cuishui joined Shuxia River from the northwest—the Gui River. It bent east to meet Zhong River, took Pan Stream, north met Maple River, and entered Xiang River at Changning. Southeast: Yangtian Lake; Tun Lake flowed out northwest, took Malun on the left, and north met Quantian River. It bent northeast as Lianpeng Stream joined flowing north, then northeast into Chenzhou. It had the abolished patrol offices at South Niubridge Market and North Sizhou Stockade. Linwu County was rated simple. It lay one hundred forty li southwest of the prefectural seat. To the north: Bayuan, also called East Mountain. To the west: Shunfeng. Southwest: Huayin. Also West Mountain—the ancient Tongbai—where Qin River rose, flowed northeast with Bei Stream on the left, and met Xiushui. It bent north as Wuxi River united with Shijiang from the west. Farther east Chitu Stream joined from the south and ran southeast into Yizhang. It had Chitu Market town. Yao Mountain stood south of the county. Lanshan County was rated simple. It lay one hundred fifty li southwest of the prefectural seat. To the north: Lanshan. To the west: Jiuyi. South: Nanfeng Pass bordering Lianzhou in Guangdong, where Zhong River rose, flowed west, bent north, and met Guishui. It rose on Jiuyi as Jiuyi River—the Shun River—ran northeast past the south of the seat, took Meng Stream on the left, bent east as Maojun united with Huajingjin from the southeast, met Lanshui, and entered Jiahe from the northeast. Southwest, the Central River entered Jianghua as Tuojiang, whose lower course joined the Xiao. It had Maojun Market town. The Daqiao Market patrol office was later moved to Linwu Garrison and renamed. Yao Mountain stood south of the county. Jiahe County was rated simple. It lay one hundred ten li southwest of the prefectural seat. To the west: Jin Ridge—that is, Lanshan. To the north: Shimen. Northwest: Shiyan Mountain. Zhong River lay south, entering from Lanshan, flowing northeast to northeast of the seat as Hanshui joined from the west, then north into Chun River at Guiyang Prefecture. Southeast, Pan Stream rose in Linwu, joined Qin Stream to the north, and also entered Chun River at Guiyang Prefecture. It had the abolished Lianglukou patrol office.
13
郴州直隸州：沖，繁，難。 隸衡永郴桂道。 舊隸湖廣布政使司。 康熙三年來屬。 北距省治六百八十里。 廣三百四十里，袤二百三十里。 北極高二十五度四十八分。 京師偏西三度四十九分三十秒。 領縣五。 東：馬嶺山。 東南：五蓋。 西南：靈壽山。 又黃岑山即騎田嶺，又名臘嶺，蓋五嶺之第二嶺也。 耒水左瀆自興寧入，西北流，梓塘江自東南來注之，東北合郴水。 出黃岑山，一名黃水，東北與沙江合。 又北受千秋水，過縣治東，北合騾溪，又北至郴江口入耒水。 耒水東北入永興，西有屯湖水，北逕棲鳳山，曰棲鳳水，又東北至永興入耒水。 南有良田市巡司。 有驛。 永興沖，繁。 州北八十里。 城內三台山。 西：高亭。 南：土富。 北：金鵝。 東北：桃源。 西南：白豹山。 耒水自州入，北合注江水，屈西過縣城西南，左納靈江，西北至森口，屯湖水合高亭水自西南來會，東北入耒陽。 東大步江，源出興寧縣，合潦溪水，東北至安仁為永樂江。 北安福、西南高亭二巡司，後廢。 有驛。 宜章沖，繁，難。 州南九十里。 北：黃岑。 東北：漏天。 南：西山。 西南：莽山。 溱水在南，亦曰武水，自臨武入，東南流，岑水合浯水自西北來注之，東南入廣東樂昌。 縣北章水，南至樂昌為羅渡水，入武水。 縣南長樂水，東北流，屈西，又東北至廣東乳源，為武陽溪，亦入武水。 東赤石、西南白沙二巡司。 有驛。 有瑤山在縣南。 興寧疲，難。 州東北八十里。 東：石牛。 西：九峰。 北：七寶。 南：浦溪山。 東南耒水自桂陽入，迤西至豐溪口，漚江自東北來注之，西北與資興江水合。 水出縣東，即古清溪，亦謂之乙陂江，又西北合雷溪水，入郴州。 縣北程江，西南至永興入耒水。 東北小江水，一名大步江，亦西北入永興。 又東春江，至酃合洣水。 有滌口巡司，州門鎮廢巡司。 桂陽簡。 州東南一百六十里。 南：屋嶺。 東：洞靈。 西：義通。 西南：大官。 東南：東嶺。 耒水在南，出耒山，西北合淥水，秀溪水自西南來會。 又西北與壽江水合，入興寧。 北漚江自桂東入，右納淇江，為北水河，西北至興寧入耒水。 縣南屋嶺水，南與藍田合，又南入仁化為恩溪。 又益將河出東嶺，左合孤山水，東北至崇義為積龍水，下流合於章水。 有益將、文明市二巡司。 山口鎮、濠村鎮有二廢巡司。 瑤山在縣南。 桂東簡。 州東北二百七十里。 西：紫台山。 南：烏春。 東：胸膛。 東北：都寮山。 又有屏水山，漚江出焉，一名澄江，南與螺川水合。 西過縣城南，桂水自西北來會，又南為嚴溪，左東溪、右白竹皆流合焉，西納雙坑水，與大江水合，南流入桂陽。 東南：泥湖山，大坪水出，入江西龍泉，為遂江水，入贛水。 左溪水亦至龍泉合遂江水。 西南有高分鎮廢巡司。
Chenzhou Direct-Controlled Prefecture was rated pivotal, busy, and difficult. It was subordinate to the Heng-Yong-Chen-Gui Circuit. Formerly under the Huguang provincial administration commission. In Kangxi 3 it came under Hunan. It lay six hundred eighty li north of the provincial seat. It measured three hundred forty li east to west and two hundred thirty li north to south. Latitude was 25°48′ N. Longitude was 3°49′30″ west of the capital. It governed five counties. To the east: Maling Mountain. Southeast: Wugai. Southwest: Lingshou Mountain. Also Huangcen Mountain was Qitian Ridge—also La Ridge—the second of the Five Ridges. A left distributary of the Lei entered from Xingning, flowed northwest as Zitang River joined from the southeast, and northeast met Chen River. It rose on Huangcen—also Huang River—and northeast met Shajiang. Farther north it took Qianqiu River, passed east of the seat, north met Luoxi, and at Chen River mouth entered the Lei. The Lei ran northeast into Yongxing; west, Tun Lake water passed north of Qifeng Mountain as Qifeng River and northeast entered the Lei at Yongxing. South stood the Liangtian Market patrol office. It had a postal station. Yongxing County was rated pivotal and busy. It lay eighty li north of the prefectural seat. Inside the city walls stood Mount Santaishan. To the west: Gaoting. To the south: Tufu. To the north: Jin'e. To the northeast: Taoyuan. To the southwest: Baobao Mountain. The Lei entered from the prefecture, north met Zhujiang River, bent west by the southwest of the seat, took Ling River on the left, and northwest at Senkou Tun Lake water met Gaoting River from the southwest, then ran northeast into Leiyang. To the east, Dabu River rose in Xingning County, joined Liaoxi River, and northeast to Anren became Yongle River. Patrol offices at Bei'anfu and Gaoting in the southwest, later abolished. It had a postal station. Yizhang County was rated pivotal, busy, and difficult. It lay ninety li south of the prefectural seat. To the north: Huangcen. To the northeast: Loutian. To the south: West Mountain. To the southwest: Mang Mountain. South lay the Qin River—also Wu River—entering from Linwu and flowing southeast as Cen River joined Yu River from the northwest, then southeast into Lechang, Guangdong. North of the county, Zhang River flowed south to Lechang as Luodu River and entered Wu River. South of the county, Changle River flowed northeast, bent west, then northeast to Ruyuan in Guangdong as Wuyang Stream and likewise entered Wu River. Patrol offices at Chishi in the east and Baisha in the southwest. It had a postal station. Yao Mountain stood south of the county. Xingning County was rated exhausted and difficult. It lay eighty li northeast of the prefectural seat. To the east: Shiniu. To the west: Jiufeng. To the north: Qibao. To the south: Puxi Mountain. Southeast, the Lei entered from Guiyang, wound west to Fengxikou as Oujiang poured in from the northeast and northwest met Zixing River water. It rose east of the county—the ancient Qing Stream, also Yipi River—then northwest joined Leixi River and entered Chenzhou. North of the county, Cheng River flowed southwest to Yongxing and entered the Lei. Northeast, Xiaojiang River—also Dabu River—likewise flowed northwest into Yongxing. Farther east, Dong River reached Ling and joined Mi River. It had the Dikou patrol office and an abolished patrol office at Zhoumen Market. Guiyang County was rated simple. It lay one hundred sixty li southeast of the prefectural seat. To the south: Wuling Ridge. To the east: Dongling. To the west: Yitong. To the southwest: Daguan. To the southeast: Dongling Ridge. The Lei lay south, rising on Lei Mountain; northwest it joined Lu River as Xiushui Stream came from the southwest to meet. Farther northwest it joined Shou River water and entered Xingning. North, Oujiang entered from Guidong, took Qi River on the right as Beishui River, and northwest at Xingning entered the Lei. South of the county, Wuling Ridge water flowed south to join Lanshan, then south into Renhua as En Stream. Farther south, Yijiang rose at Dongling Ridge, took Gushan River on the left, northeast to Chongyi as Jilong River, and downstream met Zhang River. Patrol offices at Yijiang and Wenming Market. Shankou Market and Haocun Market each had an abolished patrol office. Yao Mountain stood south of the county. Guidong County was rated simple. It lay two hundred seventy li northeast of the prefectural seat. To the west: Mount Zitai. To the south: Wuchun. To the east: Xiongtang. To the northeast: Mount Duliao. Also Mount Pingshui, where Oujiang rose—also Cheng River—south joining Luochuan River water. It passed west south of the seat as Gui River met from the northwest, then south as Yan Stream with Dong Stream left and Baizhu right all joining, west took Shuangkeng water, met Dajiang water, and flowed south into Guiyang. Southeast: Mount Nihu, where Daping River rose, entered Longquan in Jiangxi as Sui River and joined the Gan. Zuoxi River water likewise reached Longquan to join Sui River. Southwest had the abolished patrol office at Gaofen Market.
14
辰州府：沖，繁，難。 隸辰沅永靖道。 舊隸湖廣布政使司。 康熙三年來屬。 初沿明制，領州一，縣六。 乾隆元年，沅州升府，黔陽、麻陽割隸。 東距省治八百五里。 廣三百五十里，袤六百五十里。 北極高二十八度二十三分。 京師偏西六度二十二分。 領縣四。 沅陵沖，繁，難。 南：南山，一名客山。 西北：小酉。 東北：壺頭、明月。 東南：聖人山。 沅水在南，自瀘溪入，東北合藍溪，至府治西南，酉水合明溪、小酉溪自西北來注之。 東北合深溪，北屈而東，左納硃洪溪、洞庭溪，右納怡溪，迤東入桃源。 又冷溪出東南，北與三渡水合，又東北至桃源為夷望溪，入沅水。 通判駐浦市。 縣丞駐荔溪市。 有馬底鎮、船溪二巡司。 池蓬、明溪、會溪三廢巡司。 辰陽、馬底二驛。 瀘溪簡。 府西南七十里。 明，盧溪，清初改。 東：權山。 西：天橋，一名羊喬。 北：虎頭。 西南：踏湖山。 沅水在東，自辰谿合浦溪入，北至縣城南，武水合沱江水自西來注之。 水出乾州廳，曰武溪水，又名盧水也。 沅水又東北入沅陵。 西北潭溪水，西南大能水，皆流合武水。 又太平溪出西南，東南至麻陽入沅水。 南有溪洞廢巡司。 辰谿沖。 府西南一百一十里。 南：五峴。 西：大酉。 北：熊頭。 西南：房連、龍陽山。 東南：沅水自黔陽入，北過茶龍山，合麻溪水，北入漵浦。 又西北復入縣東，右納柿溪，迤西過縣城南，辰水自西來會，東北入瀘溪。 縣南龍門溪，北流合辰水。 有黃溪口巡司。 山塘驛。 有渡口、普市二鎮。 漵浦繁，疲，難。 府東南二百七十里。 東：紅旗。 東南：頓家。 西北：盧峰。 西南：大漵山。 沅水在西，右會漵水，一名雙龍江，源出縣南金字山，逕龍潭溪，進馬江自東南來注之。 屈而北，左納貓兒江，右納柿溪江，又北與龍灣江水合。 又西北流，宣陽江東北自聖人山來會，西至縣治東南，大潭水南流合焉，又西合沅水，東北入辰谿。 南有龍潭巡司。 瑤山在縣南。
Chen Prefecture was rated pivotal, busy, and difficult. It was subordinate to the Chen-Yuan-Yongjing Circuit. Formerly under the Huguang provincial administration commission. In Kangxi 3 it came under Hunan. At first it followed the Ming arrangement, governing one subordinate prefecture and six counties. In Qianlong 1 (1736) Yuanzhou was raised to prefectural status, and Qianyang and Mayang were transferred to its jurisdiction. It lay eight hundred five li east of the provincial seat. It measured three hundred fifty li east to west and six hundred fifty li north to south. Latitude was 28°23′ N. Longitude was 6°22′ west of the capital. It governed four counties. Yuanling was rated pivotal, busy, and difficult. To the south: South Mountain—also Guest Mountain. To the northwest: Xiaoyou. To the northeast: Hutou and Mingyue. To the southeast: Sage Mountain. The Yuan lay south, entering from Luxi and northeast joining Lan Stream to the prefectural seat southwest, as You River with Ming Stream and Xiaoyou Stream poured in from the northwest. Northeast it joined Shen Stream, bent north and east, took Zhuhong and Dongting streams on the left and Yi Stream on the right, and wound east into Taoyuan. Also Leng Stream rose southeast, north met Sandu River, then northeast to Taoyuan as Yiwang Stream entering the Yuan. The subprefectural judge was stationed at Pushi. The assistant magistrate was stationed at Lixi Market. Patrol offices at Madi Market and Chuan Stream. Three abolished patrol offices: Chipeng, Mingxi, and Huixi. Postal stations at Chenyang and Madi. Luxi County was rated simple. It lay seventy li southwest of the prefectural seat. Under the Ming it was Luxi; the name was changed in the early Qing. To the east: Quan Mountain. To the west: Sky Bridge—also Yangqiao. To the north: Hutou. To the southwest: Mount Tahu. The Yuan lay east, entering from Chenxi with Pu Stream, north to south of the seat, as Wu River with Tuojiang water poured in from the west. It rose in Qianzhou Department as Wuxi River—also Lu River. The Yuan again flowed northeast into Yuanling. Northwest Tanxi and southwest Daneng waters both flowed to join Wu River. Taiping Stream rose southwest, flowed southeast to Mayang, and entered the Yuan. South had the abolished Xidong patrol office. Chenxi County was rated pivotal. It lay one hundred ten li southwest of the prefectural seat. To the south: Wuxian. To the west: Dayou. To the north: Xiongtou. To the southwest: Fanglian and Longyang Mountain. Southeast: the Yuan entered from Qianyang, ran north past Chalong Mountain, took Mazi Stream, and flowed north into Xupu. It again entered the county from the northwest, took Shixi on the right, wound west south of the seat as Chen River met from the west, then flowed northeast into Luxi. South of the county, Longmen Stream flowed north to join Chen River. A Huangxikou patrol office was stationed there. Shantang postal station. Markets at Dukou and Pushi. Xupu County was rated busy, exhausted, and difficult. It lay two hundred seventy li southeast of the prefectural seat. To the east: Hongqi. To the southeast: Dunjia. To the northwest: Lufeng. To the southwest: Dawu Mountain. The Yuan lay west, taking Xushui on the right—also Shuanglong River—which rose south of the county at Jinzi Mountain, ran through Longtan Stream, and received Jinma River from the southeast. It bent north, took Mao'er River on the left and Shixi River on the right, then north joined Longwan River water. Flowing northwest, Xuanyang River met from Sage Mountain in the northeast; west to southeast of the seat, Datang water joined from the south, then west joined the Yuan and northeast entered Chenxi. A Longtan patrol office lay to the south. Yao Mountain stood south of the county.
15
沅州府：沖。 隸辰沅永靖道。 本明沅州，隸辰州府。 乾隆元年升為府。 東北距省治一千一百三十五里。 廣二百八十里，袤二百五十五里。 北極高二十七度二十三分。 京師偏西七度零三分三十秒。 領縣三。 芷江沖，繁，難。 倚。 乾隆元年，以州地置。 北：明山。 東北：武陽。 東：花山。 東南：高明。 西南：羅山。 西北：米公山。 潕水即無水，自晃州入，東北流，左納柳林溪、粟米溪，屈東南，過府治南，楊溪東流屈北注之，與五郎溪合。 東屈而南，豐溪水自東北來入，東南入黔陽。 西南：中和溪，出晃州東南，至黔陽入沅水。 縣丞治榆樹灣，懷化、便水二巡司。 晃州、便水、羅舊、懷化四驛。 黔陽沖。 府東南九十里。 本隸辰州府。 乾隆元年來屬。 南：赤寶。 北：紫霄。 東：龍標。 東北：鉤崖。 東南：羅公山。 沅水在西，自會同入，東至托口寨，左合中和溪，右合渠水，屈東北至縣城西，與潕水會。 其會流處曰清江口，即古無口也。 又東南流，錯入會同，迤東北復入縣東，供溪水北流西屈注之。 水出綏寧，其上流為𦰡溪水，東北入辰谿。 東：石橋、安江二巡司，道光十二年廢。 瑤山在東南。 麻陽難。 府西北一百二十里。 本隸辰州府。 乾隆元年來屬。 北：紗帽。 南：西晃。 東：苞茅。 東南有齊天。 東北：雄山，其下有雄關。 辰水在南，一名麻陽江，自貴州銅仁入，東與密粟溪水合。 左納銅信溪，右納石橋溪，過縣治東南，屈而北，樂濠溪自西北來注之，又東合太平溪，至辰谿入沅水。 縣丞治岩門寨，有高村巡司。 岩門驛。
Yuanzhou Prefecture was rated pivotal. It was subordinate to the Chen-Yuan-Yongjing Circuit. Originally Ming Yuanzhou, it had been subordinate to Chen Prefecture. In Qianlong 1 (1736) it was raised to prefectural status. It lay one thousand one hundred thirty-five li northeast of the provincial seat. It measured two hundred eighty li east to west and two hundred fifty-five li north to south. Latitude was 27°23′ N. Longitude was 7°03′30″ west of the capital. It governed three counties. Zhijiang County was rated pivotal, busy, and difficult. Attached to the prefectural seat. In Qianlong 1 it was established on the former subprefecture seat. To the north: Mount Ming. To the northeast: Wuyang. To the east: Huashan. To the southeast: Gaoming. To the southwest: Mount Luo. To the northwest: Mount Migong. Wu River—the Wushui—entered from Huangzhou, flowed northeast, took Liulin and Sumi streams on the left, bent southeast past the prefectural seat, received Yang Stream bending back from the east, and joined Wulang Stream. It bent east and south as Fengxi entered from the northeast, then flowed southeast into Qianyang. Southwest: Zhonghe Stream, rising southeast of Huangzhou, entered the Yuan at Qianyang. The assistant magistrate was stationed at Yushu Bay; patrol offices at Huaihua and Bianshui. Postal stations at Huangzhou, Bianshui, Luojiu, and Huaihua. Qianyang County was rated pivotal. It lay ninety li southeast of the prefectural seat. Formerly under Chen Prefecture. In Qianlong 1 it was transferred here. To the south: Chibao. To the north: Zixiao. To the east: Longbiao. To the northeast: Gouya. To the southeast: Mount Luogong. The Yuan lay west, entering from Huitong, east to Tuokou Stockade, taking Zhonghe Stream left and Qu River right, bending northeast to west of the seat to meet Wu River. The confluence was Qingjiangkou—the ancient Wukou. It again flowed southeast, strayed into Huitong, wound northeast back into the county east, as Gongxi River bent north and west to pour in. Rising in Suining, its upper stream was Naxi Creek, flowing northeast into Chenxi. East: Shiqiao and Anjiang patrol offices, abolished in Daoguang 12. Yao Mountain lay in the southeast. Mayang County was rated difficult. It lay one hundred twenty li northwest of the prefectural seat. Formerly under Chen Prefecture. In Qianlong 1 it was transferred here. To the north: Shamao. To the south: Xihuang. To the east: Baomao. Qitian lay to the southeast. Northeast: Mount Xiong, with Xiong Pass below. Chen River lay south—also Mayang River—entering from Tongren in Guizhou and east joining Mili Stream. It took Tongxin left and Shiqiao right, passed southeast of the seat, bent north as Lehao Stream entered from the northwest, east joined Taiping Stream, and at Chenxi entered the Yuan. The assistant magistrate was stationed at Yanmen Stockade; a Gaocun patrol office was stationed there. Yanmen postal station.
16
永順府：難。 隸辰沅永靖道。 明為永順等處軍民宣慰使司。 領土州三：南渭、施溶、上溪； 長官司六：臘惹峒、麥著黃峒、驢遲峒、施溶峒、白崖峒、田家峒。 隸湖廣都司。 雍正四年改流官置廳，隸辰州府。 七年升為府。 東南距省治一千八十里。 廣五百里，袤五百五十里。 北極高二十九度二分，京師偏西六度四十分。 領縣四。 永順難。 倚。 本永順宣慰司地。 雍正七年置，治猛峒。 東南距舊司治三十里。 東：飛霞山、賀虎。 東北：蟠龍。 東南：羊峰。 西北：萬笏。 酉水中源自保靖合入逝溪，東與喇集溪合。 溪出龍山，曰汝池河，東南過府治西南，小溪水自北來注之，南與牛路河合，入酉水。 酉水又南屈而東，左納施溶溪，入沅陵。 東南：明溪，亦南至沅陵入酉水。 東北：上洞河，出縣北，過十萬坪入桑植，是為澧水南源。 府經歷駐劉家寨。 王村巡司。 田家峒廢司。 驛三：王村、毛坪、高望界。 龍山簡。 府西北二百二十里。 雍正七年析永順宣慰司地置，治麂皮壩。 乾隆元年又省大喇土司地入焉。 南：洛塔。 東南：鐵爐。 西南：八面山。 酉水在南，即北河，又名更始水。 三源，其北源曰白水河，自湖北宣恩緣界流入，南逕縣治西北，中界湖北來鳳縣，又南流，果利河自東北來注之。 又南與皮渡河合，為卯洞河，西南錯入酉陽州。 其中源曰邑梅河，出秀山，北流東屈來會，又東復入縣西南境。 其右岸則保靖縣界也。 東與洗車河合，入保靖。 東南：汝池河，至永順入酉水。 有隆頭巡司。 保靖難。 府西南一百四十里。 本保靖宣慰司地。 領五寨、筸子坪二長官司。 雍正四年改流官置廳，隸辰州府。 七年改為縣來屬，治茅坪，西南距舊司治半里。 西：煙霞、洛浦。 北：雲台。 南：呂洞山。 酉水自四川酉陽州入，迤東流，左界龍山，又東屈而南。 其南源牛角河，出貴州松桃廳，東流屈北來會。 又東過縣治北，左納蒙沖溪。 又東與白溪水合，入永順。 張家寨巡司。 保靖、白棲關二站。 桑植簡。 府東北一百二十里。 本桑植安撫司地。 領美坪等苗峒凡十有八。 雍正四年，改流官置廳，隸岳州府。 七年改為縣，析慈利縣安福所地益之。 治安福所城。 乾隆元年，復省上峒、下峒、茅岡三土司地入焉。 北：天星。 東：陽岐。 東南：簸箕山。 澧水三源：西北源曰夾石河，出栗山坡，東南為綠水河，又東至兩河口； 南源上峒河，自永順北流來會，又東與涼水口河合； 河出西北七眼泉，是為澧水北源。 東屈而南，至縣治西北，長酉水自東北來注之。 又南入永定。 又有繩子溪，出東北紅花嶺，東南至慈利入漊水。 有下峒廢巡司。
Yongshun Prefecture was rated difficult. It was subordinate to the Chen-Yuan-Yongjing Circuit. Under the Ming it was the Yongshun Military-Civilian Pacification Superintendent Office. It governed three native prefectures: Nanwei, Shirong, and Shangxi; Six native chieftain's offices: Lare, Maizhu Huang, Lvchi, Shirong, Baiya, and Tianjia stockades. It was subordinate to the Huguang regional command. In Yongzheng 4 (1726) it was placed under regular officials as a department subordinate to Chen Prefecture. In Yongzheng 7 it was raised to prefectural status. It lay one thousand eighty li southeast of the provincial seat. It measured five hundred li east to west and five hundred fifty li north to south. Latitude was 29°02′ N; longitude was 6°40′ west of the capital. It governed four counties. Yongshun County was rated difficult. Attached to the prefectural seat. Formerly the seat of the Yongshun pacification superintendent office. Established in Yongzheng 7 (1729), with the seat at Mengdong. It lay thirty li southeast of the old pacification seat. To the east: Mount Feixia and Hehu. To the northeast: Panlong. To the southeast: Yangfeng. To the northwest: Wanhu. You River headwaters from Baojing joined Shixi, which east met Laji Stream. A stream rose in Longshan as Ruchi River, ran southeast past southwest of the seat, received Xiaoxi from the north, south joined Niulu River, and entered You River. You River bent south and east, took Shirong Stream on the left, and entered Yuanling. Southeast: Ming Stream likewise ran south to Yuanling and entered You River. Northeast: Shangdong River, rising north of the county, passed Shiwanping into Sangzhi as the Li River's southern source. The prefectural registrar was stationed at Liujia Stockade.
