Wangcun patrol office. The abolished Tianjia stockade office. Three postal stations: Wangcun, Maoping, and Gaowangjie. Longshan County was rated simple. It lay two hundred twenty li northwest of the prefectural seat. Established in Yongzheng 7 (1729) from Yongshun pacification superintendent territory, with the seat at Jipi Dam. In Qianlong 1 (1736) Dala native chieftain territory was also merged in. To the south: Luota. To the southeast: Tielu. To the southwest: Bamian Mountain. The You River lay south—the North River, also Gengshi River. Three sources: the northern was Baishui River, entering from Xuan'en in Hubei along the border, south past northwest of the seat, mid-course bordering Laifeng in Hubei, south again as Guoli River entered from the northeast. Farther south it united with Pidu River as Maodong River, southwest straying into Youyang Prefecture. The middle source was Yimei River, rising in Xiushan, flowing north and bending east to join, then east again into the county southwest. Its right bank was Baojing County's border. East it united with Xiche River and entered Baojing. Southeast: Ruchi River ran to Yongshun and entered You River. It had the Longtou patrol office. Baojing County was rated difficult. It lay one hundred forty li southwest of the prefectural seat. Formerly the seat of the Baojing pacification superintendent office. It governed the native chieftain's offices of Wuzhai and Ganziping. In Yongzheng 4 (1726) it was placed under regular officials as a department subordinate to Chen Prefecture. In Yongzheng 7 it became a county under this prefecture, with the seat at Maoping, half a li southwest of the old pacification seat. To the west: Yanxia and Luopu. To the north: Yuntai. To the south: Lüdong Mountain. You River entered from Youyang in Sichuan, wound east with Longshan on the left, then bent east and south. Its southern source Niujiao River rose in Songtao in Guizhou, flowed east and bent north to join. Farther east it passed north of the seat, taking Mengchong Stream on the left. Farther east it united with Baixi River and entered Yongshun. Zhangjia Stockade patrol office. Relay stations at Baojing and Baiqi Pass. Sangzhi County was rated simple. It lay one hundred twenty li northeast of the prefectural seat. Formerly the seat of the Sangzhi pacification commissioner office. It governed eighteen Miao stockades including Meiping. In Yongzheng 4 (1726) it was placed under regular officials as a department subordinate to Yue Prefecture. In Yongzheng 7 it became a county, augmented by territory carved from Anfu subprefecture in Cili. The seat was at Anfu subprefecture city. In Qianlong 1 (1736) the territories of Shangdong, Xiadong, and Maogang native chieftains were again merged in. To the north: Tianxing. To the east: Yangqi. To the southeast: Boqi Mountain. The Li had three sources: the northwest was Jiashi River from Lishan Slope, southeast becoming Lüshui River, east to Lianghekou; The southern source Shangdong River flowed north from Yongshun to join, east united with Liangshuikou River; A river rose from Qiyan Spring in the northwest as the Li's northern source. It bent east and south to northwest of the seat as Chang You River entered from the northeast. Farther south it entered Yongding. Shengzi Stream also rose on Honghualing in the northeast and southeast to Cili entered the Lao River. It had the abolished Xiadong patrol office.
17
靖州直隸州：繁，難。 隸辰沅永靖道。 本隸湖廣布政使司。 康熙三年來屬。 雍正五年，割天柱隸貴州黎平。 東北距省治一千六十里。 廣三百七十里。 袤三百六十里。 北極高二十度三十五分。 京師偏西七度。 領縣三。 南：侍郎。 東：鴻陵。 西：飛山。 西北：艮山。 西南：青蘿。 渠水在東，古謂之敘水，自通道入，北至縣治東南，右納老鴉溪，左納潩溪，西北入會同。 西南有四鄉河，源出貴州開泰，東北至通道入渠水。 有零溪巡司。 會同難。 州北九十里。 北：岩屋。 西北：八仙。 東北：金龍。 沅水在西北，自貴州天柱縣入，東北錯入黔陽。 又東逕縣東北，巫水合若水溪自東南來注之，入於黔陽。 西：渠水自靖州入，北逕縣治西北，右納平川，與吉朗溪合。 水出貴州開泰，又名郎江水，西北至黔陽入沅水。 西南堡子巡司。 洪江司，廢。 通道難。 州南九十里。 東：玉柱。 東南：福湖。 又佛子山，渠水出焉，西北過犁嘴山，播陽河自西南來會。 河出開泰，曰六衝江，又名洪州江也。 北與四鄉河水合，北至縣治西南，臨川河入焉，又東北入靖州。 西南有播陽廢巡司。 綏寧繁，難。 州東南一百二十里。 北：寶鼎。 東北：藍溪。 又有楓門山，巫水在西，即洪江，古謂之運水，又曰雄溪，自城步入，西北至界溪口，蒔竹水自南來注之。 又北流為竹舟江，西北至會同入沅水。 又蓼溪水，源出東北雞籠山，東為武陽水，又東北入武岡州，是為高沙市水也。 南：長平水自城步入，西流，右納駕馬溪，又西與雙江水合，西北至通道合渠水。 有青陂、雙江二巡司。
Jingzhou Direct-Controlled Prefecture was rated busy and difficult. It was subordinate to the Chen-Yuan-Yongjing Circuit. Formerly under the Huguang Regional Administration Commission. In Kangxi 3 it came under Hunan. In Yongzheng 5 (1727) Tianzhu was transferred to Liping in Guizhou. It lay one thousand sixty li northeast of the provincial seat. It measured three hundred seventy li east to west. It measured three hundred sixty li north to south. Latitude was 20°35′ N. Longitude was 7° west of the capital. It governed three counties. To the south: Shilang. To the east: Hongling. To the west: Feishan. To the northwest: Genshan. To the southwest: Qingluo. Qu River lay east—anciently Xu River—entering from Tongdao, north to southeast of the seat, taking Laoya Stream right and Weixi left, northwest into Huitong. Southwest: Sixiang River, rising in Kaitai in Guizhou, northeast to Tongdao entered Qu River. It had the Lingxi patrol office. Huitong County was rated difficult. It lay ninety li north of the prefectural seat. To the north: Yanwu. To the northwest: Baxian. To the northeast: Jinlong. Yuan River lay northwest, entering from Tianzhu in Guizhou, northeast straying into Qianyang. Farther east it passed northeast of the county as Wu River united with Ruoshui Stream from the southeast and entered Qianyang. West: Qu River entered from Jingzhou, north past northwest of the seat, took Pingchuan on the right and united with Jilang Stream. It rose in Kaitai in Guizhou—also Langjiang River—northwest to Qianyang entered the Yuan. Southwest: Baozi patrol office. The Hongjiang office was abolished. Tongdao County was rated difficult. It lay ninety li south of the prefectural seat. To the east: Yuzhu. To the southeast: Fuhu. Mount Fozi was where Qu River rose; northwest past Lizui Mountain Boyang River met from the southwest. Rising in Kaitai, it was Liuchong River—also Hongzhou River. North it united with Sixiang River, north to southwest of the seat as Linchuan River entered, northeast into Jingzhou. Southwest had the abolished Boyang patrol office. Suining County was rated busy and difficult. It lay one hundred twenty li southeast of the prefectural seat. To the north: Baoding. To the northeast: Lanxi. Mount Fengmen also stood there; Wu River lay west—Hongjiang, anciently Yun River or Xiong Stream—entering from Chengbu, northwest to Jiexikou as Shizhu River entered from the south. Farther north it became Zhuzhou River, northwest to Huitong entered the Yuan. Liaoxi River also rose on Jilong Mountain in the northeast, east became Wuyang River, northeast into Wugang as Gaoshashi River. South: Changping River entered from Chengbu, flowed west, took Jima Stream on the right, west united with Shuangjiang River, northwest to Tongdao met Qu River. It had the Qingpi and Shuangjiang patrol offices.
18
乾州直隸廳：繁，難。 隸辰沅永靖道。 明為鎮溪軍民千戶所，隸辰州府瀘溪縣。 康熙三十九年改為乾州。 四十七年置廳，治鎮溪所城，仍隸辰州府。 嘉慶元年升直隸廳。 轄苗寨一百一十有五。 東北距省治九百六十五里。 廣一百二十里，袤九十里。 北極高二十八度十二分。 京師偏西六度五十九分。 東：鎮溪。 西：武山，武水出焉，一名武溪，又名盧溪，迤東過廳治西，屈而南，萬溶江自鳳凰廳北流東屈注之。 又東與鎮溪水合，東南入瀘溪。 有河溪、乾州二廢巡司。 鎮溪、喜鵲二營，皆嘉慶二年置。
Qianzhou Direct-Control Department was rated busy and difficult. It was subordinate to the Chen-Yuan-Yongjing Circuit. Under the Ming it was the Zhenxi Military-Civilian Thousand-Household Office, subordinate to Luxi County in Chen Prefecture. In Kangxi 39 (1700) it was renamed Qianzhou. In Kangxi 47 (1708) a department was established at Zhenxi guard city, still under Chen Prefecture. In Jiaqing 1 (1796) it was raised to a direct-controlled department. It governed 115 Miao stockades. It lay 965 li northeast of the provincial seat. It measured 120 li east to west and 90 li north to south. Latitude was 28°12′ N. Longitude was 6°59′ west of the capital. To the east: Zhenxi. To the west: Mount Wu, where Wu River rose—also Wuxi or Luxi—wound east past the seat's west side, bent south, and received Wanrong River from Fenghuang bending in from the north. Farther east it united with Zhenxi River and flowed southeast into Luxi. It had the abolished patrol offices of Hexi and Qianzhou. Zhenxi and Xique garrisons were both established in Jiaqing 2 (1797).
19
鳳凰直隸廳：繁，難。 鎮筸總兵、辰沅永靖道駐。 明為五寨、筸子坪二長官司，隸保靖宣慰使司。 康熙四十三年，改流官置通判，辰沅靖道僉事徙駐。 雍正四年改鳳凰營。 乾隆五十二年改廳，升通判為同知。 嘉慶元年升直隸廳。 轄紅苗寨一百有五。 東北距省治一千五十里。 廣一百八十四里，袤一百二十里。 北極高二十七度五十三分。 京師偏西七度三分。 南：南華山。 西：鳳凰山，上有鳳凰營，又有鳳凰營司巡檢，後廢。 東南：觀景。 南：二華。 西南：都督。 沱江自貴州銅仁入，迤東北流，烏巢江自北來注之。 東過廳治北，又東北入於瀘溪，是為武水最南源也。 又，萬溶江源出西北天星砦山，東屈而北，左納龍爪溪，西北至乾州合武水。 西南：樂濠溪，東南至麻陽入辰水。 祐營，知事駐。 得勝營、五寨站有巡司。
Fenghuang Direct-Control Department was rated busy and difficult. The Zhen'ao regional commander and Chen-Yuan-Yongjing Circuit were stationed here. Under the Ming it comprised the native chieftain's offices of Wuzhai and Ganziping, under the Baojing pacification superintendent. In Kangxi 43 (1704) it was placed under regular officials with a subprefectural judge, and the Chen-Yuan-Jing Circuit vice commissioner moved his station here. In Yongzheng 4 (1726) it was renamed Fenghuang Garrison. In Qianlong 52 (1787) it became a department and its subprefectural judge was raised to associate prefect. In Jiaqing 1 (1796) it was raised to a direct-controlled department. It governed 105 Red Miao stockades. It lay 1,050 li northeast of the provincial seat. It measured 184 li east to west and 120 li north to south. Latitude was 27°53′ N. Longitude was 7°3′ west of the capital. To the south: Nanhua Mountain. To the west: Fenghuang Mountain, atop which stood Fenghuang Garrison; it also had a Fenghuang Garrison inspection sub-office, later abolished. To the southeast: Guanjing. To the south: Erhua. To the southwest: Dudu. Tuojiang River entered from Tongren in Guizhou and wound northeast, receiving Wuchao River from the north. Flowing east past the seat's north side, it continued northeast into Luxi as the southernmost source of Wu River. Wanrong River also rose northwest at Tianxing Stockade Mountain, bent east and north, took Longzhao Stream on the left, and at Qianzhou joined Wu River from the northwest. Southwest: Lehao Stream flowed southeast to Mayang and entered Chen River. You Garrison, where the administration secretary was posted. Desheng Garrison; Wuzhai relay station had a patrol office.
20
永綏直隸廳：繁，難。 隸辰沅永靖道。 綏靖總兵駐。 明，鎮溪千戶所、崇山衛地，隸辰州府瀘溪縣。 雍正元年置廳吉多營，仍隸辰州府。 嘉慶元年升直隸廳。 七年移治花園堡。 轄紅苗寨二百二十有八。 東北距省治一千一百五十九里。 廣九十里，袤一百五十五里。 北極高二十八度四十三分。 京師偏西七度。 南：大排吾山。 西：苞茅。 西南：蠟爾。 牛角河即酉水南源，自貴州松桃廳緣界流入，北至茶洞城，其左岸則四川酉陽州界也。 屈而東北，界保靖縣。 東過廳治北，臘爾堡河自西南來注之，東北入保靖。 西南：高岩河，源出犀牛潭，入乾州為鎮溪，入武水。 茶洞，廢知事，隆團、排補二砦廢司。 有花園砦。
Yongsui Direct-Control Department was rated busy and difficult. It was subordinate to the Chen-Yuan-Yongjing Circuit. The Suijing regional commander was stationed here. Under the Ming it was Zhenxi Thousand-Household Office and Chongshan Guard territory, subordinate to Luxi County in Chen Prefecture. In Yongzheng 1 (1723) a department was established at Jiduo Garrison, still under Chen Prefecture. In Jiaqing 1 (1796) it was raised to a direct-controlled department. In Jiaqing 7 (1802) the seat moved to Huayuan Fort. It governed 228 Red Miao stockades. It lay 1,159 li northeast of the provincial seat. It measured 90 li east to west and 155 li north to south. Latitude was 28°43′ N. Longitude was 7° west of the capital. To the south: Dapaiwu Mountain. To the west: Baomao. To the southwest: La'er. Niujiao River—the southern source of You River—entered along the border from Songtao in Guizhou, north to Chadong city, with Youyang in Sichuan on its left bank. It bent northeast along the border with Baojing County. Flowing east past the seat's north side, it received La'er Fort River from the southwest and entered Baojing to the northeast. Southwest: Gaoyan River rose at Xiniu Pool, became Zhenxi at Qianzhou, and joined Wu River. Chadong had an abolished administration secretary; Longtuan and Paubu stockades had abolished sub-offices. It had Huayuan Stockade.
21
晃州直隸廳：沖。 隸辰沅永靖道。 本芷江晃州堡地，屬沅州府。 嘉慶二十二年析置直隸廳，移涼傘通判治焉。 東北距省治一千二百四十五里。 廣五十二里，袤一百四十五里。 北極高二十七度二分。 京師偏西七度二十二分。 西：龍溪。 西南：尖坡。 東南：寶駿山。 潕水在南，一名無水，又名㵲水。 上流曰鎮陽江，自貴州玉屏入，東北與龍溪合。 過廳治南，左納木多溪，東流會平溪，東北入芷江。 東南：中和溪，一名羅岩江，亦東北流入芷江。 晃州、涼傘二巡司。 有驛。
Huangzhou Direct-Control Department was rated pivotal. It was subordinate to the Chen-Yuan-Yongjing Circuit. It was formerly Huangzhou Fort in Zhijiang, under Yuan Prefecture. In Jiaqing 22 (1817) it was split off as a direct-controlled department and the Liangsan subprefectural judge was relocated there. It lay 1,245 li northeast of the provincial seat. It measured 52 li east to west and 145 li north to south. Latitude was 27°2′ N. Longitude was 7°22′ west of the capital. To the west: Longxi. To the southwest: Jianpo. To the southeast: Baojun Mountain. Wu River lay to the south—also Wushui, also called Yi River. Its upper course was Zhenyang River, entering from Yuping in Guizhou and joining Longxi to the northeast. It passed south of the seat, took Muduo Stream on the left, flowed east to meet Pingxi, and entered Zhijiang to the northeast. Southeast: Zhonghe Stream—also Luoyan River—also flowed northeast into Zhijiang. Patrol offices at Huangzhou and Liangsan. It had a postal station.
